title: Every view and character is several times over §21.3's triangle and draw-call budgets
evidence: Measured headless with the prototype's own code (scratchpad/analysis/3dp/out/diorama_probe.json): realm view 163,324–219,184 triangles in 1,149–1,264 draw calls; heist 225,558 in 940; universe map 676,192 in 1,207. Characters (3dp/out/measure_all.json): 10,408–181,534 triangles at hero resolution, 2,880–76,096 at the diorama's game resolution 0.019 (Featherkin 47,644 = body 12,720 + accessories 34,924 in 100 meshes), 15–233 meshes each; seven kinds add 2–7 fur shells (creature modules 'shells:'). Buildings are inside (1,172–2,556; 3dp/out/kit.json). §21.3 (doc:10466): characters 3,000–6,000, buildings 2,000–8,000, a realm 25,000–40,000, under 150 draw calls. §23.5 has no row for it.
rec: Enforce budgets in the export harness (segment caps + per-kind sculpt step + accessories merged into the skin; Featherkin reached 12,576 automatically, the rest needs the cape as a few cards). Owner decides whether the Character screen's single close-up may use a hero mesh above 6,000. Add a §23.5 row: designs over budget, build follows §21.3.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §21.3 (doc:10466) sets the budgets: characters 3,000–6,000 triangles, buildings 2,000–8,000, a whole realm 25,000–40,000, under 150 draw calls. The reader's headless probe (3dp/out/diorama_probe.json) has 8 runs: realm 163,324–219,184 triangles in 1,149–1,264 calls, heist 225,558/940, scout 206,854/769, universe 676,192/1,207. The per-kind character counts (Archivist 181,534 at hero step; Unmade 2,880 at 0.019) are in 3dp/out/measure_all.log. measure_all.json has since been overwritten with the capped re-runs (Featherkin 22,596 at 0.019), so the cited file does not hold the uncapped numbers. Nothing in §23.5 covers it, and no register item mentions triangles or draw calls. A decision is needed (whether the Character screen may use a hero mesh), so the grade stays significant.
corrected: Every diorama view is several times over §21.3's realm triangle budget (realm 163,324–219,184; heist 225,558; scout 206,854; map 676,192) and its 150-draw-call cap (769–1,416 calls). The 43 sculpted characters are 10,408–181,534 triangles at hero step and 2,880–76,096 at the diorama's 0.019 step, against 3,000–6,000, in 15–233 meshes. The diorama's own chibi stand-ins (2,226) and its buildings (1,172–2,556) are within budget. The uncapped character figures are in 3dp/out/measure_all.log and census_table.md, not measure_all.json, which now holds the capped runs. §23.5 has no row for this.

title: Characters are drawn physically based; the diorama's toon is four-step with world-space outlines in the wrong ink
evidence: Creature bodies: MeshPhysicalMaterial with sheen and a Fresnel shader patch (creature_kit.js:62, 71); accessories with clearcoat, metal, transmission, iridescence (creature_parts.js:4, 21, 36); hero pages use ACES tone mapping and a PMREM environment, no outline (Featherkin_Hero.html). Portrait/observatory/scout/land PNGs are renders of that look (images/world_*.png). Diorama: four-step gradient [62,140,215,255] (realm_diorama.js:485), +10% saturation on every colour (:519), back-face hull outlines scaled in world units in #140A18 (:486, :520). §21.3 (doc:10462): three-step ramp, violet shadows, soft rim, 1.5-pixel ink outlines; §21.2: ink #221C3A.
rec: One Godot toon shader family for everything (vertex-colour albedo with baked AO, 3-step ramp in light(), violet shadow tint, rim, hemisphere ambient) and a clip-space 1.5-px outline next_pass in #221C3A; re-render portraits from the imported models; record in §23.5 that the build follows §21.3.
verdict_why: Every citation checks out. realm_diorama.js:485 builds a four-entry gradient [62,140,215,255], so the ramp has four steps, not §21.3's three. :519 applies offsetHSL(0,.1,0) to every colour. :486 and :520 draw outlines as back-face hulls in #140A18, scaled in world units; §21.3 (doc:10462) asks for 1.5-pixel ink outlines and §21.2 sets ink to #221C3A. Creature bodies use MeshPhysicalMaterial with sheen and a Fresnel patch (creature_kit.js:62, 71). Accessories use clearcoat, metalness and transmission (creature_parts.js:4, 21, 36), and iridescence in 8 modules. Featherkin_Hero.html uses ACESFilmicToneMapping and a PMREMGenerator and draws no outline. images/world_portraits_featherkin.png is a smooth physically based render with no outline. §21.3 also says 'The toon, outline … shaders already exist from the mock-ups', which is true only of three.js versions that differ from its own spec. This is a rule the document states, so the document wins. §23.5 has no row for it.

title: No 3D model has the guard form (sash and lantern) although §23.5 says every sheet has it
evidence: §23.5 (doc:11570): each kind has 'a guard form with sash and lantern'; §21.6 (doc:10652): 'As guards, ruleborn add a sash and a small lantern.' The sheets' 'As a guard' chip only relabels the view: Featherkin_dc.html:169 sets 'AS A GUARD · SASH + LANTERN'; none of the 43 *_Rig.html pages has a 'guard' form branch (Featherkin_Rig.html handles only echo :86, hush :91, spark :92; the one 'guard' token is in the Archivist's page, unrelated). The diorama's guards are one primitive kind with a cone helmet for every role (realm_diorama.js:143). The characters report confirmed the guard form from the label only.
rec: Correct §23.5's sentence; make sash and lantern as shared accessory pieces per size band (plus §21.6's role accessories so a guard's role reads, §12.8) in the character task.
verdict_why: Confirmed. Featherkin_dc.html:151 offers a 'guard' chip, and :169 only changes the label to 'AS A GUARD · SASH + LANTERN'. :51 and :177 pass form=guard to the Rig page. In Featherkin_Rig.html:89–92, FORM='guard' matches none of the hush, spark or echo branches, so the page draws the base form. A grep of all 43 *_Rig.html pages and every creature module finds no sash or guard geometry; the only 'sash' is the Archivist's own robe sash. §23.5 (doc:11570) says each kind has 'a guard form with sash and lantern', and §21.6 (doc:10652) requires it. One detail is wrong: the diorama's guards (realm_diorama.js:143) do carry a lantern glow sprite. They have a cone helmet but no sash.
corrected: No character sheet's 3D draws the guard form. The 'As a guard' chip relabels the view and renders the base form (Featherkin_dc.html:169; Featherkin_Rig.html:89–92 has no guard branch), so §23.5's sentence that every kind has 'a guard form with sash and lantern' is wrong. The diorama's guards are one chibi kind with a cone helmet and a lantern glow for every role, and no sash (realm_diorama.js:143).

title: Forms change colour and glow only; Hush is colour alone, which §21.6 calls a failed form, and no form adds an accessory
evidence: §21.6 (doc:10658–10660): each form 'changes a ruleborn's pattern, glow and one accessory in its note's colour' and 'A form that only differs by colour has failed'. Featherkin_Rig.html:91 Hush remaps the body's vertex colours by luminance and nothing else; :92 Spark sets emissive #6A2208 and adds ember sprites with point lights; :86 Echo adds a translucent copy 0.3 s behind; no form adds an accessory. The squint test renders the base form only (Featherkin_dc.html:134, sil=1&clip=idle). §23.5 (doc:11570) says each sheet has 'its three forms and a squint test'.
rec: Design one note accessory each for Hush, Spark and Echo (per size band, shared across kinds, '54 forms need 18 models') and a pattern mask per note in the toon shader; squint-test every form; correct §23.5.
verdict_why: Confirmed. Featherkin_Rig.html:91: Hush remaps the body's vertex colours by luminance and changes nothing else. :92: Spark sets emissive #6A2208 at 0.35 and adds ember sprites with point lights. :86: Echo adds a translucent magenta copy of the rig. No branch adds an accessory or changes the pattern. Featherkin_dc.html:134 runs the squint test with sil=1&clip=idle and no form, so only the base form is tested. §21.6 (doc:10658–10660) requires each form to change pattern, glow and one accessory, and says a form that differs only by colour has failed. The title's 'colour and glow only' leaves out Echo's ghost copy.
corrected: Each form changes one thing: Hush the colours, Spark a glow with ember sprites, Echo a trailing translucent copy (Featherkin_Rig.html:91, :92, :86). None changes the pattern or adds an accessory in its note's colour, as §21.6 requires. Hush is colour alone, which §21.6 calls a failed form. The squint test renders only the base form (Featherkin_dc.html:134). §23.5's 'its three forms and a squint test' therefore overstates what meets §21.6.

title: Several 3D models are not the height §21.6 and their own sheets state
evidence: Measured in the idle pose at each module's own GAME_SCALE (3dp/out/heights.json): Prism Mite 0.76 m vs 0.5 m (§21.6 doc:10695; sheet header '0.5 m'; prismmite.js:78 GAME_SCALE=1.35); Glass Golem 1.39 m body, 1.53 m with crest, vs 1.2 m; Stormhound 0.98 vs 0.9; Sparkwright 0.86 vs 0.8; Sages Tinkerer 0.97, Wanderer 1.27, Gardener 1.32 vs §21.1's 'about 1.5'. The diorama ignores GAME_SCALE and scales every kind to one height (realm_diorama.js:602). §23.5 says heights match; the characters report checked header chips only.
rec: Derive each import scale from §21.6's height column (§21.1 for Sages) and test it in the export check; owner states whether crests, flames and baskets count in the height.
verdict_why: heights.json confirms the figures: Prism Mite 0.757 m at GAME_SCALE 1.35 (prismmite.js:78) against §21.6's 0.5 m (doc:10695) and the sheet's '0.5 m' chip (Prism_Mite_dc.html:29). Glass Golem is 1.39 m (body) to 1.53 m against 1.2 m. Stormhound is 0.98 and Sparkwright 0.86. Two caveats. No code says GAME_SCALE is metres; that is inferred because eight kinds land on §21.6's heights at it. The Tinkerer is 'small' in §21.6, so 0.97 m may be intended. realm_diorama.js:602 scales hero rigs to a per-family target of 0.64–0.76 units (×1.05 in the heist), not to one height. The document's heights win and the build only needs an import scale, so the grade is minor.
corrected: At each module's GAME_SCALE, which matches §21.6 for eight kinds and so reads as metres, Prism Mite stands 0.76 m against 0.5 m and Glass Golem 1.39–1.53 m against 1.2 m. Stormhound (0.98 against 0.9) and Sparkwright (0.86 against 0.8) are 8–9% tall. The Wanderer (1.27 m) and Gardener (1.32 m) are short of §21.1's 'Sages about 1.5'; the Tinkerer (0.97 m) is 'small' in §21.6. §23.5's 'height' match is therefore wrong for at least Prism Mite and Glass Golem. The diorama ignores GAME_SCALE and fits each family to 0.64–0.76 units (realm_diorama.js:602).

title: A replay cannot be drawn with the right creatures: no kind, form or outfit reaches the view
evidence: Raider and Guard carry role and no kind (sim/src/lib.rs:447–462, 584–614); RulebornReplay crew()/guards() return role, position, gait, state (client/ext/src/lib.rs:341–373); the heist record's crew is one byte (sim/src/replay.rs:147); a post is (row, x, y) (sim/src/island.rs:87–91). §24 renders the deterministic replay into a 15-second clip on the phone and §13 lets the defender watch it; forms (§21.6) and outfits (§22) are what those must show.
rec: Add an appearance block (kind, form, outfit per crew member and per posted guard, ~4 bytes an actor) stored with the heist and island bundle beside — not inside — §24.11's four simulation inputs, and expose it in the replay API.
verdict_why: The gap is confirmed. Guard and Raider carry only a role (sim/src/lib.rs:447–462, 584–637), and sim/src/lib.rs:255–259 says 'The simulation's crew and guards are roles, not ruleborn'. Heist.crew is a count (sim/src/replay.rs:147). World::on_ground assigns roles by a fixed order (CREW[i % len], lib.rs:770–771). Post is (row, x, y) (island.rs:87–91). crew() and guards() in client/ext/src/lib.rs:341–373 return no kind. The recommendation is wrong, though: kind and form are not view-only. §11.2's abilities and resistances, and §11.10's form quirks (noticed 10% later, +5% power, returns once after a knockout), change the simulation. They therefore belong inside §24.11's inputs (the heist record and the island bundle), not beside them; only the outfit is view-only. No register item covers this.
corrected: The heist record holds a crew count, and the simulation assigns roles by a fixed order. The island's posts hold a role row and a tile, and the replay API returns roles and positions only. Nothing records which ruleborn (kind), form or outfit raided or guarded, so neither a replay nor §24's 15-second clip can draw the right creatures. Kind and form also change the simulation (§11.2 abilities and resistances, §11.10 quirks), so they must enter the heist record and the island bundle as simulation inputs (§24.11). Only the outfit can sit beside them as view data.

title: §21.3's budgets do not add up, and its frame-rate floor contradicts §24
evidence: (a) At the per-asset floors an outer realm in a heist with three staffed producers, a Hearth, a Storehouse, three Guardian Posts and a Law Pylon (9 buildings × 2,000 = 18,000), a crew of five, a guard per post and a worker per producer (11 characters × 3,000 = 33,000) is 51,000 triangles before terrain, wards and effects, against 'a whole realm 25,000 to 40,000' (doc:10466). (b) §21.3 (doc:10468): '60 frames a second on iPhone 12 and newer, never below 30 on the oldest supported phone'; §24: '60 frames a second is a floor' and reference device 'a mid-range 4 GB Android at 60 Hz'.
rec: State the realm budget at the camera's distance with LODs (or raise it to ~60,000 for the heist), and make §24's reference device and 60 fps floor the single performance rule.
verdict_why: (a) The arithmetic holds. §5.2 gives an outer realm 1 each of well, spring and garden, plus up to 3 guard posts. At §21.3's per-asset floors, 9 buildings × 2,000 plus 11 characters × 3,000 is 51,000 triangles, over the 40,000 'whole realm' ceiling (doc:10466). The document mentions no LODs. Q8 (guards per post) is still open, which affects the character count. (b) §21.3 (doc:10468) says 60 fps on iPhone 12 and newer and 'never below 30 on the oldest supported phone'. §24 (doc:11706) says '60 frames a second is a floor, because 30 measurably harms performance', and its reference device (doc:11709) is a mid-range 4 GB Android, not an iPhone. That is a real contradiction. No register item covers either part; C7 and C16 are about tick rate and clock length.

title: §24's 25 ms touch-to-picture drag budget is unmeasured and not reachable as written on a 60 Hz phone
evidence: §24 (doc:11706): 'Under 25 ms from touch to picture for dragging'. One 60 Hz frame is 16.7 ms; the engine renders after reading input and the Android compositor presents at the next refresh, so a drag typically shows two or more frames later. No section, test (grep client/tests, tools) or register item defines how it is measured, whether prediction counts, or what a miss triggers.
rec: Define it as measured on the reference device with a high-speed camera; allow 1–2 frames of drag extrapolation; read touches unaccumulated and as late as possible; keep the 3D frame under ~8 ms; add the measurement to TC.8.
verdict_why: §24 (doc:11706) reads: 'Under 25 ms from touch to picture for dragging'. A grep of client/tests, client/scripts, tools/ and tools/roadmap.py finds no latency measurement and no definition. No register item mentions it. The technical point is sound: one 60 Hz frame is 16.7 ms, and Android shows a frame at least one refresh after it is drawn. Touch-to-display on 60 Hz phones is typically well above 25 ms without prediction. The rule cannot be tested as written, so a decision is needed.

title: The height of one terrain level in metres is unstated
evidence: §6.1 (doc:1160): 'four heights (0 to 3)'; §21.1 fixes the tile at one metre but no level height. The prototype draws levels as 2.1-unit blocks on 3.9-unit cells, 0.54 of a tile (realm_diorama.js:280, :308), and has no heights at all in heist mode. The 3D world must place raised tiles, ramps, stairs and climb/leap animations at a fixed height.
rec: Adopt 0.5 m a level (the design's ratio) and state it in §21.1.
verdict_why: §6.1 (doc:1160) gives four heights (0 to 3), and §21.1 (doc:10408) fixes the tile at one metre. A grep for metre statements finds no height per level; doc:7251's 'a level higher sees a metre further' is about sight range, not elevation. realm_diorama.js:280 sets DF.S=3.9, and :308–311 builds HL=2.1 blocks per level, in the defence overlay only. Under §23.5's rule, where the document is silent the design is adopted (about 0.54 of a tile), so this is a row for the adopted table, not a conflict.
corrected: No section states how tall one terrain level is. The design's defence overlay draws 2.1 units per level on 3.9-unit cells, about 0.54 m a level at 1 tile = 1 m. Under §23.5's silence rule that ratio is adopted unless stated otherwise, and it should be listed in §23.5's adopted table or stated in §21.1.

title: Bringing the art into Godot is budgeted nowhere: not in §26.8 and not in the roadmap
evidence: §26.8's phase table (doc:12503–12594) has no row for the 3D world, characters, shaders or effects; tools/roadmap.py TC.7 'The design from Claude Design' covers 'Tokens and components, and the screens' layouts' only; §26.3 lists a character artist, but the sheets are now code. The pipeline (export harness, toon kit, world from the replay, characters with forms/springs, appearance block) sizes at roughly 16–25 agent runs.
rec: Add SC tasks TC.15 art export harness, TC.16 toon kit, TC.17 world from the replay, TC.18 characters in full, TC.19 appearance in the replay, and a §26.8 row for the art pass.
verdict_why: tools/roadmap.py:1152–1156: TC.7 'The design from Claude Design' covers 'Tokens and components, and the screens' layouts' only. No SC task covers the 3D world, the toon shaders, importing the characters or effects. The roadmap's T3.4 text even says 'the diorama is the art pass' without giving it a task. In §26.8's phase table (doc:12503–12594), the only rendering is phase 3's 'render a replay' in a first playable. No row covers the 3D diorama, characters, shaders or effects. §26.3 gives character art to a contractor, but the sheets are generated code, so bringing them in is engineering. The 16–25-run size is the reader's own estimate.
corrected: Neither §26.8 nor tools/roadmap.py budgets bringing Screens v3's 3D into Godot. §26.8's only rendering line is phase 3's 'render a replay' in a first playable. The roadmap's TC.7 covers tokens, components and layouts, and TC.8 covers devices. Exporting the art, the toon and outline shaders, the 3D world drawn from the replay, and characters with forms and the guard form have no task and no runs.

title: Screens v3 supplies a fraction of §21.9's asset list (extends C24)
evidence: §21.9 (doc:11018–11036): 68 building looks (17 types × 4), 24 law signatures, 8 harmony + 4 dissonance + 12 chord effects. The diorama models 8 building types at one look each (Hearth, Star Well, 'Aether Loom', Garden, Guard Post, Vault, Ward, Spire; makeB2 output identical at levels 1, 5 and 9 — 3dp/out/kit.json; realm_diorama.js:691–880): no Anchor Stone, Storehouse, Law Pylon, Nursery, Library, Resonance Lab, Observatory, Beacon or Visitor's Dock, no level 7–9 crystal-and-gold or level-10 crown looks (§21.5); 3D law effects for 9 of 24 laws (lawFX, :1312–1332). The 39 terrain pieces (:316–365) and the four links (:1167–1195) are complete.
rec: Have the export harness's asset manifest list §21.9 row by row with its source (exported, to make, contractor) so the remaining art is a tracked number; cross-reference C24.
verdict_why: §21.9 (doc:11018–11036) is confirmed. The diorama's building code handles eight types: hearth, starwell, loom, garden, guard, vault, ward and spire. lawFX (realm_diorama.js:1312–1332) covers nine laws. Two parts are mis-stated. Buildings do change with level: dress() (:981–987) adds a lamp post, a flag from level 3, and banners and a finial from level 6. That is still not §21.5's four looks (wood and rough stone, dressed stone with school trims, crystal and gold, a level-10 crown). And 'extends C24' is wrong: C24 is about §26.1's 16-against-17 building count. The nearest register item is C8 (§21.9's building-look count after the Library), and neither covers how much art the designs supply. It is significant because the realm view must tell pylons apart (§23.5 realm-view row), and the Law Pylon has no model.
corrected: Screens v3's diorama models 8 of the 17 building types: Hearth, Star Well, 'Aether Loom' (the Aether Spring), Garden, Guardian Post, Vault, Ward and Spire. It has no Anchor Stone, Storehouse, Law Pylon, Nursery, Library, Resonance Lab, Observatory, Beacon or Visitor's Dock. Its level changes are a flag from level 3 and banners and a finial from level 6 (realm_diorama.js:981–987), not §21.5's four looks. It has 3D effects for 9 of §21.9's 24 law signatures. The terrain kit and the four links are complete. This relates to C8 (the §21.9 building-look count), not C24.

title: v3.6 empties the Twinned's gift: it doubles abilities it does not have
evidence: v3.6 §11.8 (doc:6250-6251) changed v3.4's 'Acts twice: every ability fires two times.' to 'Acts twice: every ability it fires, fires two times. Its crew's abilities fire once.' (v36/diffs.txt §11.8). Paradox-born 'have no role in 11.1' (doc:6257), and §11.11 says 'These cards are the one home for every ability' (doc:6337); only the 18 kinds have cards. The Twinned therefore fires no ability, and the narrowed gift does nothing. The sheet's version gave it an effect: 'Every ability it or its crew fires, fires two times' (creatures/Twinned_dc.html:173).
rec: The owner writes what 'acts twice' doubles, as a rule-sheet change (§7.3). Options: the Twinned's own hits and loading against its shared 120 health and 80 carry, or one two-use ability of its own with the 10-second lockout. The Twinned should not be built or balanced until this is written.
verdict_why: Confirmed. v3.6 §11.8 (doc:6249-6251) reads 'Acts twice: every ability it fires, fires two times. Its crew's abilities fire once.' (the v3.4 text was 'every ability fires two times', v36/diffs.txt:31-32). Paradox-born 'have no role in 11.1' (doc:6257). §11.11 says its cards are 'the one home for every ability' (doc:6337), and it has cards only for the 18 kinds. No trait or Sage power is something the Twinned 'fires'. So the narrowed gift has nothing to double. The sheet's gift is 'Every ability it or its crew fires, fires two times', with Best at 'Doubling a key ability at the Vault' (creatures/Twinned_dc.html:173). §23.5's Twinned row records the narrowing, not that the result is empty. Paradox-born ship at launch (§21.9 'paradox-born ... 3'), so a launch gift has no effect until the owner decides one.

title: Paradox-born lack guard behaviour, a school mark, gift rule sheets, sounds and a forms decision
evidence: §12.8 (doc:7034): 'Guards are the defender's own ruleborn … and their role decides how they behave'; paradox-born have no role (doc:6257), yet every paradox-born sheet has an 'As a guard' form. §21.6 requires every ruleborn to wear its school colour and mark; the sheets say 'Legendary: no school badge; its paradox is its mark' (Reverser_dc.html:182). §11.11 requires every ability to have a named-parameter rule sheet and every character a sound; the gifts have neither. §11.10 counts 54 forms as 18 kinds × 3; the sheets give paradox-born Hush, Spark and Echo forms with quirks (lines 153-156), and the Echo quirk is a revival. v3.6 makes the Twinned's 120 health and 80 carry 'shared', but the sheet shows '2 × 60' and '2 × 40' (Twinned_dc.html:174). sim/src/lib.rs:244-253 keys every crew stat to Role.
rec: Record one owner decision for each point: guard behaviour (or 'paradox-born do not guard'), school mark (or adopt the paradox mark in §23.5), rule-sheet lines and sounds for the gifts, forms yes or no. Model the Twinned as one sim body with shared pools; the second silhouette is cosmetic. Screens show 120 and 80.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §12.8 (doc:7034): 'their role decides how they behave', and the behaviour table lists the five roles only. Paradox-born have no role (doc:6257), yet Reverser, Twinned and Unmade each offer an 'As a guard' form (Twinned_dc.html:151, same line in the others). Each sheet also offers Hush, Spark and Echo forms with quirks (+5% power, a revival), at lines 153-156. §11.10 counts 54 = 18 kinds x 3, but its first sentence says 'Every ruleborn hatches in a form shaped by the laws around its Nursery', and paradox-born are born at a Nursery, so the document is ambiguous. The cards have no 'Rule sheet' and no 'Sounds like' line (Twinned_dc.html:173), unlike every §11.11 card. The doc says '120, shared by its two bodies' and '80, shared', but the sheet shows '2 x 60' and '2 x 40' (Twinned_dc.html:174). sim/src/lib.rs:244-253 is the Role enum, and crew stats are looked up by role. One sub-claim is mis-stated: paradoxes carry no school (§7.5, doc:2179-2201), so §21.6's school colour and mark rule has nothing to apply to. 'Its paradox is its mark' (Reverser_dc.html:182) fills a silence, so it is something to list as adopted, not a broken rule. §23.5 adopts only the paradox-born numbers, sizes and proportions.
corrected: Paradox-born have no role, so §12.8 gives them no guard behaviour, yet every paradox-born sheet has an 'As a guard' form. Their sheets add Hush, Spark and Echo forms with quirks, and §11.10 both counts 54 forms (18 x 3) and says every ruleborn born at a Nursery takes a form, so whether paradox-born get forms needs an owner decision. The gifts have no §11.11-style rule-sheet line or sound. The Twinned sheet shows '2 x 60' and '2 x 40' where §11.8 says 120 and 80 are shared. Paradoxes have no school (§7.5), so the sheets' 'no school badge; its paradox is its mark' fills a silence and should be listed as adopted in §23.5, not treated as a §21.6 breach.

title: Work loops: §21.6 asks for one per building (three); sheets have one, mostly the home habit
evidence: §21.6 (doc:10656) ends its animation list with '…nap, and one work loop per building'. Only the Star Well, Aether Spring and Garden take workers (§10.1, doc:4738), so each kind needs three work loops. Each sheet has a single 'work' clip (line 160). Only Featherkin and Skyskipper (Star Well) and Mossbear (Garden) work a building. The other 15 reuse their §11.11 at-home habit, e.g. Glass_Golem_dc.html:160 'Watch the sky', Prism_Mite_dc.html:160 'Plays with itself', Soulmender_dc.html:160 'Sits with the loser'. §11.11's habit is a separate requirement that §21.6's list omits. The knock-out clip's 'dizzy stars, then a puff of petals' appears in no sheet's description; the rig code was not checked. So §23.5's 'each has the fifteen animations of 21.6' overstates what exists.

title: 28% of the design's text runs fail §21.8's contrast, and there is no agreed way to measure outlined text
evidence: Measured over the 1,049 visible text runs on all 28 Gameplay screens, against the pixels under each run in a render with the glyphs made transparent, using colour_check.gd's formulas: 19% are under 4.5:1 at the median background, 22% at the worst decile, 24% under the APCA level for their size and weight, 28% fail one or the other. Causes: white marks on light fills (113 runs, median 2.77:1; 85 of them tab and section badges on red #FF8A9A to #E2364E, green or violet at 1.8-2.8:1, screens_main.js:664-665). The law card title 'Stillness' in white Marcellus 25 on cyan is 1.55:1. Tertiary #8A7AA8 is about 4.5:1 but Lc 34. Secondary #B8A8D8/#B8A8E0 is 7-9:1 but Lc 57-59. On parchment, #7A5A34 is 3.04, #2F7A45 3.99, #8A6A4A 4.22. Red words #E2536B on night are 4.19:1, Lc 35. Heist crew names drawn in school colours over the 3D ground are 1.4-3.1:1, though each has a hard ink shadow that reads at 5.8-10.3:1. State in §21.8 how outlined text is measured (proposal: an ink outline of at least 1.5 pt, or 12% of the size, counts as the fill's background). verdict_why: Re-computed from ds_out/contrast.json: 1,049 runs. 201 (19%) are under 4.5:1 at the median background, 234 (22%) at the worst decile, 250 (24%) under the APCA level and 292 (28%) fail one or the other. 113 white runs fail. title: Interface transitions run 300-550 ms with overshoot, against §21.8's 150-250 ms easing out

title: The design draws only a night backdrop; §21.2's sky follows local time

title: “Was this worth your time?” is two-point in the design, five-point in the gates, per session in §20.3 and per heist in §23.2
evidence: §19.5: “one tap” and the gate “4.3 out of 5 or higher” (doc 9418); launch gate “4 out of 5” (doc 12087, 11161); §20.3 and §19.5: every session; §23.2: on every heist result. server/src/telemetry.mjs 84 validates an integer 1–5 and 51 counts one per session. Design: Yes / Not really (screens_main.markup.html 860), which cannot produce a five-point average.
rec: One row of five one-tap points on the result, asked once a session (first or last result), never required; amend §23.2 or §20.3 so they agree on frequency.
verdict_why: The document's text is as claimed. §19.5 has "one tap", "Every session, live" and the fun gate "4.3 out of 5 or higher" (9402, 9418). The soft-to-global launch gate is "at least 4 out of 5" (11161, 12087). §20.3 says "Every session can end with ... a one-tap rating" (10221). §23.2 puts it on the heist result (11233). The server validates integers 1-5 and allows one per session (server/src/telemetry.mjs:51-53, 84). G29 covers counting per session but not the scale or the result-versus-session placement. The 4.3 and 4 figures belong to two different gates, so they do not contradict each other.

Separately, §19.5 and §20.3 ask the question once a session while §23.2 places it on every heist result. The two gates use different thresholds on purpose and do not contradict each other.

title: “Alarm” names two things; the design reads an alert as a realm-alarm level, the sim as a Clean/Loud flag
evidence: §12.9 Clean “No alarm”, Loud “Alarm raised”; §12.17 Alerted “raises the alarm”; but the realm alarm climbs once every 30 s whatever the crew does (§12.6, §12.17), so “no alarm” cannot mean it. sim reads a flag set on Alerted (sim/src/lib.rs 702–704, 3181). Design adds a level per alert: “HEARD YOU · Alarm +1” and alarmAdd += 1 (realm_diorama.js 218; screens_main.js 113), and its result shows Clean “0 / 6 alarm” at 2:14 (screens_main.js 645), impossible under §12.17. Not in the register.

verdict_why: §12.9 says Clean is "No alarm" and Loud is "Alarm raised". In §12.17 the Alerted state "raises the alarm", yet the realm-alarm ladder in §12.17 (and §12.6) climbs only by time, discovered bodies and bell posts. The word therefore covers two things. The sim already reads it as a separate flag (lib.rs:701-704, 3177-3181, with the comment "Not the realm alarm"). The design adds a realm level on every alert: realm_diorama.js:218 has `H.alarmAdd+=1`, screens_main.js:113 adds it to h.alarm, and the banner reads "Alarm +1 · they are looking" (markup ~806). That is a mechanic §12.17 does not have. The design's Clean result shows "2:14 · 0 / 6 alarm", which is impossible because its own HUD climbs one level every 30 s (screens_main.js:461). Not in the register or §23.5.

title: The design’s Vault phase is automatic, Carrier-only and shows no cracking progress

The build already orders crack and load by tap (heist_controller.gd:88-93). Not listed in §23.5.

title: No law pylons exist in the heist world
evidence: realm_diorama.js contains no pylon code; the heist diorama (122–238) draws houses, wells, Spire, Vault, wards and guards only. §12.6: breaking a pylon is a crossing decision and gives a page; “A pylon shows its law’s school colour and that law’s own glyph … and a tag names its law the first time the crew sees it”. §23.5’s Realm view row covers pylons looking alike, not their absence from the heist.
rec: Design a pylon per school (realm-view work) and draw it in the heist with its first-sight tag; the build’s sim already supports BREAK.
verdict_why: realm_diorama.js contains no pylon object at all (0 matches). The heist reuses the realm island and adds crew, guards, wards, the Vault and the Spire. Screenshots (hr_shots/heist_t40.png, Gameplay_04_Realm_view.png) show no law pylon, only wards with four stones and a gem. The design's 'Pylon' in the build tray is a 'spire' type that "Links wards; guards hear alarms" (screens_main.js:156), not a law pylon. §12.6 requires pylons in each law's school colour and glyph, and §15.3 a first-sight tag "in every heist". §23.5's Realm view row says pylons "look alike", which assumes they exist. It does not record that the heist has none.
corrected: The design draws no law pylon anywhere: the heist and the realm view share the island, and its only 'Pylon' is a ward-linking defence building. §12.6's pylon look and §15.3's first-sight tag therefore have no design. §23.5's Realm view row only says pylons look alike.
existing: none (G5 is about pylon count, health and placement in the document)

title: §12.7’s controls give no way to stop a crew member or drop loot
evidence: §12.6: “whether to drop loot to run faster” is an escape decision; §12.19 prices dropping; standing still matters for tall grass and Stillness (§12.17). §12.7’s table and §12.18’s held taps offer neither. Build has Halt and Drop-half buttons outside §12.7 (client/scripts/heist_screen.gd 308–309); the design has neither.
rec: A held tap on a crew member offers Stop, Drop half, Drop all, extending §12.18’s held-tap rule with no new control or mechanic; write it into §12.18.
verdict_why: §12.6 names "whether to drop loot to run faster" as an escape decision, and §12.19 prices dropping. Yet §12.7's table and §12.18's held taps (gait on open ground, actions on wall, ledge or vent) offer no Drop and no Stop. The design has none either: the markup's "drop" hits are CSS drop-shadow. The build adds Halt and Drop-half buttons outside §12.7's list (client/scripts/heist_screen.gd:308-309), next to a gait button, so the build's control count already exceeds §12.7's set. Not in the register. Re-graded significant because a named decision has no control and a choice is needed.

title: The eight-control cap against open wheels, the law card on request and pause in ruins
evidence: With the Sage wheel open the design has eleven live buttons (hr_shots/heist_sage.png; wheel at z-index 6 over live portraits, screens_main.js 472). §15.3 wants the law card “on request” after the third time; §20.8 a pause “at any time in ruins and rehearsals”; each adds a ninth control beside five portraits, Sage, Cast and Get out.
rec: Wheels and held-tap menus are modal (the rest inert while open); the law card opens from a held tap on a law chip; pause is the system back gesture or the clock in ruins/rehearsals; the doc says which.
verdict_why: §12.7 caps tappable things at eight, but its own Sage row opens a three-power wheel. The design's wheel (zIndex 6, screens_main.js:462) leaves the portrait row (zIndex 5, :467) and the other buttons live, so 11 targets are tappable at once (hr_shots/heist_sage.png). §15.3 wants the law card "only on request" after the third time, and §20.8 allows pause "at any time in ruins and rehearsals". Neither says which control does it. The design's law chips are pointer-events:none. Nothing in the register mentions wheels or pause. The line citation should be screens_main.js:462/477, not 472.

title: The design adds a start-of-heist grace and slow-motion on every alert
evidence: Guards cannot notice anything for the first 4.2 s, 1.6 s after the player can act (realm_diorama.js 214, intro 2.6 s at 198); the world runs at 25% for 1.3 s at each alert (218) while the prototype clock keeps running on its own timer (screens_main.js 188). Neither is in §12.17.
rec: No grace: tick 0 starts after the entry card. Slow-motion is the owner’s call; if kept it slows the simulation and its clock together, applies to every player regardless of reduced motion, and appears in replays.
verdict_why: realm_diorama.js:214 sets `if(now-H.t0<4200)best=0;` and the intro lasts 2.6 s (:198). Slow motion: `H.slowU=now+1300` on an alert (:218) and `dt*0.25` while slow (:195). The prototype clock runs on its own setInterval (screens_main.js:188). The claim is overstated in one respect: only the sight-based gain (`best`) is zeroed during the 4.2 s. Running within 4 tiles and the crack ping still raise suspicion (:212-213). §12.17 has no grace period.
corrected: For the first 4.2 s the design's guards cannot gain suspicion by sight, though they still hear running and cracking (realm_diorama.js:212-214). That is 1.6 s past the 2.6 s intro. Each alert also runs the world at 25% for 1.3 s while the prototype clock keeps its own timer. §12.17 contains neither.

title: Vault contents: hidden until it opens (§12.12, §19.16) or always on screen (§12.6, §12.19, §21.8)
evidence: §12.12: “the Vault’s contents are only revealed when it opens”; §19.16: “A Vault shows its size before its contents”. §12.6/§12.19/§21.8 keep “what is left to load” always on screen. Design shows “Left 2,600” from the first second (markup 799); build likewise (client/scripts/heist_hud.gd 51).
rec: Before the Vault opens, Left shows the free scout’s rough loot estimate (§12.4) or “?”; the exact figure once open. Amend §12.6’s always-on list.
verdict_why: These are the document's own words, and they conflict. §12.12 (line 7141): "the Vault's contents are only revealed when it opens". §19.16 (9801): "A Vault shows its size before its contents". §12.6 (6998), §12.19 (7376) and §21.8 (11001) keep "what is left to load" always on screen. The design shows Left 2,600 from the start (markup ~799; initHeist left:2600). The build shows the exposed share at all times (client/scripts/heist_hud.gd:51). Not in the register.

title: The result’s one thing to try is voiced as the Archivist’s tip, and the Clean tip is not tied to its moment
evidence: “The Archivist · try this” on every result (screens_main.markup.html 843) merges §15.3’s Archivist’s tips (“At most one per session … can be turned off”) with “One thing to try: a single suggestion on the heist result”. Clean’s tip “Kofi’s universe is two realms deep. Same crew, a bigger haul.” (screens_main.js 638) suggests another target, not something “tied to that moment” (§12.13).
rec: Label it “Try this” (or let the Sage that came voice it without the tip limits) and tie every variant to its moment.
verdict_why: Every result labels the tip "The Archivist · try this" (markup ~843), which merges §15.3's Archivist's tips (at most one per session, can be turned off) with the separate "One thing to try" row. The Clean tip "Kofi's universe is two realms deep. Same crew, a bigger haul." (screens_main.js TIP.Clean) does not follow from its moment ("Your crew crossed the open ledge while the Scout faced away"), against §12.13's "a single suggestion tied to that moment". The Archivist is the Sage chosen in the planner, so the voice is defensible. The untied Clean tip is the concrete fault.

title: No highlight clip to share from the result
evidence: §17.6: “After each heist the game cuts a 15-second vertical clip of its best moment, with the laws labelled, ready to share in one tap”; §20.7: 13–15 share in-game only. The design’s result (markup 824–869) has no share entry; the Share sheet exists separately.
rec: A share button on the moment card opening the Share sheet, following the age band; the clip rendered on the device from the replay (§24 Clips).
verdict_why: §17.6 (line 8936): "After each heist the game cuts a 15-second vertical clip ... ready to share in one tap". The design's result has no share entry. The Share sheet (screen 27) is reached only from the menu entry ('share','Share','Clips and challenges'). §23.2's result must-show does not list sharing, so this is an omission against §17.6, not against a must-show. Not in the register.

title: Insight from heists has no amount, and the result has no line for it
evidence: §9.1: Insight is earned from “Successful heists, Lab discoveries, anomalies”; §12.1 lists Insight as a reason to raid; §11.7 levels Sages with it. No section gives a per-heist amount; the design’s result and the server’s settle answer (server/src/service.mjs 784) carry none. Not in the register.
rec: A number per outcome in §9.1 or §12.1 (from the economy model), then a tile on the result; strays and season stars (which have rules) also get a line.
verdict_why: §9.1 lists Insight sources ("Successful heists, Lab discoveries, anomalies"), §12.1 lists Insight as a raid reward, and §9.x prices Sage levels at 15×1.13^(level−1) Insight. §14.1 says Insight arrives "as described in 7.6 and 11.7", but neither section gives an income amount. The server's settle answer has no Insight (server/src/service.mjs:784). The economy model lists Sage levels as NOT_MODELLED (tools/economy_model/rerun.py:39). The design's result has no Insight line. Not in the register. Re-graded significant: Sage levelling cannot be built or balanced without a figure, so a decision is needed.

title: Study chips show what is added, not what is left, and non-Foiled results omit first-met laws and pylon pages
evidence: §14.8: “Every album, law, level and track shows “2 pages to go””. The study chips show “+2” only (screens_main.markup.html 850). §7.6: first meeting adds the law with 1 page and breaking a pylon gives a page; §12.6: every law met joins the Codex whatever the outcome; the design mentions the Codex only on Foiled (screens_main.js 650).
rec: “+2 · 6 to go” on each chip; a line listing laws met for the first time and pylon pages on every outcome.
verdict_why: The study chips show only "+2" (markup ~850), while §14.8 says every law shows "2 pages to go". That half holds. The second half is weaker. §7.6 and §12.6 make first-met laws join the Codex and pylons give pages whatever the outcome, and the design mentions the Codex only on Foiled. But no section (§23.2's result row included) requires the result to list them, so that part is a suggestion, not a rule the design breaks.
corrected: The result's study chips show the pages added (+2) but not what is left for that law, against §14.8's "2 pages to go" rule. Listing first-met laws and pylon pages on every outcome is a recommendation: §7.6 and §12.6 make them happen but do not require the result to show them.

title: The result has one variant; target kinds and validation states need about ten
evidence: Design draws only a matchmade player target. Doc variants: echo (no Renown, G30), generated fallback (labelled, §12.22), Trace (no fee, listed in §23.5), drifting ruin (no Renown, §12.10), echo trial (style score, Insight, cosmetics), friendly heist (no haul; friend earns pages, §12.11), challenge link; §24.12 states: confirming, refused, lease expired, cap reached (“a clear message saying so”); server’s renownCounted (F40) and haul.cappedBy (G20) (server/src/service.mjs 784); first-session result shows a law unlocked and two strays (§16).
rec: A variant table in the screen spec carried by a ResultPresenter; reward numbers revealed only once the server answers online, confirming offline (“nothing is ever confirmed before it is real”).
verdict_why: The design draws only Clean, Loud, Partial and Foiled for a matchmade player target. The document defines other cases: echoes (§12.3; no Renown is the register's G30 reading, not doc text), generated fallbacks labelled "at the point of attack" (§12.22), Trace (already a §23.5 row), drifting ruins without Renown (§12.10), echo trials (§12.10), friendly heists (§12.11), and §24.12's "marked as confirming", lease expired and cap-reached "clear message" states. The build's result screen already handles confirming and refused (client/scripts/result_screen.gd:59-102). The server returns renownCounted (service.mjs:784). This is a coverage gap the build can fill from the document, so minor rather than significant.
corrected: The design draws one target kind. Echo, generated, ruin, trial, friendly and challenge targets, plus §24.12's confirming, refused, expired and capped states, have no designed result. The document defines what each pays. The build already shows confirming and refused (result_screen.gd).

title: §23.5’s claim that the heist and result “already follow this document” does not hold
evidence: §23.5 (doc 11418): “The heist screen, the planner, the result … already follow this document; these are the differences that remain”, listing only Role health, Trace, Text size, Landscape and the notes for these screens. Unlisted: automatic Vault phase (realm_diorama.js 208), alarm +1 on alert (218), five abilities ready and no pip numbers (§12.6, §21.8), ability effects (171, 168), grace (214), two-point worth (markup 860), “tune the targets” text (861), easier copy of a player’s universe (screens_main.js 656), Clean at 0/6 alarm (645), idle-crew and “nothing else is lost” texts (658, 650).
rec: v3.7’s §23.5 lists these differences, or the register carries them as the designs’ open differences, before the heist and result are built from the designs.
verdict_why: §23.5 (line 11418) says the heist, planner and result "already follow this document", and the unlisted differences show that does not hold. Beyond findings 4-6, 10 and 3, this finding adds items checked here. All five abilities can be ready at once, with no four-ready rule (screens_main.js:191 useAbility), against §12.6. The pips carry no number beside them, against §21.8. Emberling's Burst stuns guards within 1.6 (realm_diorama.js:171), where §11.2 has triple Power to wards and pylons within 1 tile. Tidewalker gets a ×1.25 speed boost (:168, :204) where §11.2 has "nothing slows it". The result reads "Idle crew of 5 ready" after all five rest. Foiled reads "nothing else is lost" although the entry fee is paid to the defender (§12.9).

title: Leaving the app mid-heist is not specified
evidence: §20.8 allows pausing only in ruins and rehearsals; §24.12 runs a heist on the device; a phone call or app switch stops the app. Nothing says whether a heist against a player pauses, continues or ends when the app leaves the foreground, or what happens to a lease left mid-heist. Build: client/scripts/heist_screen.gd _process (217) simply stops stepping.
rec: The simulation pauses with the app and resumes after a three-second countdown; a heist abandoned past the lease is submitted as played so far; write it into §24.12.
verdict_why: Nothing in the document covers backgrounding mid-heist: a grep for background, foreground, interrupt or phone call finds no rule. §20.8 allows pause only in ruins and rehearsals. §24.12's lease runs a day. The client has no NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_* handling. heist_screen.gd:216-222 _process just advances by delta, so it stops while the app is suspended. What happens on resume is not handled either: a large delta may catch up many ticks at once. Not in the register (G29 defines a session as the device's foreground).

title: Realm view's build tray and diorama add mechanics and break five rules (producers per realm, Storehouse, worker slots, typed guard posts, invented wards, a ward-linking Pylon)
evidence: screens_main.js:156 TRAYS: Star Well '3 / 4', Aether Loom '2 / 3', Essence Garden '2 / 4'; Storehouse 'Protects loot from raids' '1 / 2' (offered in the Heart); Ward 'Rune circle that raises the alarm'; Pylon 'Links wards; guards hear alarms'; Scout/Warden/Breaker post 1,500/1,800/2,100 'breaks crew shields'; Grate 'Traps a crew member for 3 s'; Lantern 'Lights up hiding spots'. realm_diorama.js:88-89 HEART_L/GEN place two Star Wells in the Heart and three Wells/three Gardens/two Looms in outer realms; :1275 `slots:b.res?2:0`, :1289 `wk>=2`. Captured: hrs/shots4/realm_tray_build.png, realm_tray_defence.png, realm_selected.png (level-7 Star Well 'WORKERS 1/2'). Document: §5.8 'A realm holds one Star Well, one Aether Spring and one Garden'; §9.4/§10.2 Storehouse 'Outer realms; 1 per realm … fully exposed'; §10.1 worker slots 1/2/3 by level; §10.2 Guardian Post 'One ruleborn stands at each'; §10.3 six wards (Gravity Well, Crystal Wall, Time Snare, Static Coil, Thorn Hedge, Lantern Glare); no ward-linking building (universe-wide alarm is the law Whispers). None of these is in §23.5's table.
rec: Build the trays from §10.2/§10.3 data via the server's 'room' and content/buildings.json, wards.json; add rows to §23.5 'Where the screens differ' so the design file is corrected (or the owner writes any wanted mechanic into §10 first).
verdict_why: Confirmed. screens_main.js:156 TRAYS has Star Well '3 / 4', Aether Loom '2 / 3', Essence Garden '2 / 4', Storehouse 'Protects loot from raids.' '1 / 2', Ward 'Rune circle that raises the alarm.', Pylon (key 'spire') 'Links wards; guards hear alarms.', Scout/Warden/Breaker post at 1,500/1,800/2,100 ('breaks crew shields'), Grate 'Traps a crew member for 3 s.' and Lantern 'Lights up hiding spots.'. The tray is the same in every realm, so the Storehouse is also offered in the Heart (realm_tray_build capture is in the Heart). realm_diorama.js:88-89 puts two Star Wells in the Heart and up to three Wells, three Gardens and two Looms in outer realms. :1275 has `slots:b.res?2:0` and :1289 has `wk>=2`, so a level-7 Star Well shows WORKERS 1/2. The document says otherwise: §5.8 allows one Star Well, one Aether Spring and one Garden per realm. §10.2 puts the Storehouse in 'Outer realms; 1 per realm' with '4,000 Starlight and Essence each; fully exposed', and §9.4 also calls it fully exposed. §10.1 gives 1/2/3 worker slots by level. §10.2's Guardian Post has 'One ruleborn stands at each', so posts are not typed. §10.3 has exactly six wards. The only universe-wide alarm is the law Whispers. §23.5's only realm-view row is about things looking alike. These are added mechanics, which §23.5 forbids, and §23.5's table does not list them.
corrected: Correct, and there is one more rule it breaks: Hearths. §10.2 says 'Hearth: Every realm; 1 per realm'. The design puts three Hearths in the Heart and up to four in an outer realm (realm_diorama.js:88-89), and the tray shows Hearth '5 / 8'. So the count is more than five rules. The tray also describes the Storehouse as protecting loot, but §9.4 says it is fully exposed.

title: Build timers and a two-builder limit in the realm view, against §10's instant building
evidence: realm_diorama.js:1291 startUpgrade: `if(this.isl.buildings.filter(x=>x.up).length>=2)…return false; b.up={t0:…,dur:10000+b.lv*1500}`; markup screens_main.markup.html:541 'Upgrading to {{ selV.upTo }}' with a countdown; selActs show seconds left (screens_main.js:151). §10 intro: 'There are no build timers: building and upgrading are instant, and the pace comes from resources and from the Spire's level'.
rec: Instant upgrades at §10.2's price (as server/src/universe.mjs already does); record in §23.5.
verdict_why: Confirmed. realm_diorama.js:1291 startUpgrade refuses a third upgrade while two are running, and it sets `b.up={t0,dur:10000+b.lv*1500}`. screens_main.markup.html:541 shows 'Upgrading to …' with a countdown, and screens_main.js:151 shows the seconds left on the upgrade button. The realm view also shows a builders-free chip 'x/2' (bFree, screens_main.js:184). The §10 intro says 'There are no build timers: building and upgrading are instant'. The upgrade timer and the builder cap are added mechanics, and §23.5 does not list them.

title: Realm view's terrain tray contradicts §6.1-6.2 (features, effects, prices, budget)
evidence: screens_main.js:157: Pond 'Swimmers ignore; slows raiders' 4 pts; Stream 6 pts; Hill 'Blocks sight lines' 5; Cliff 'A wall raiders must climb' 8; Hedge 'Cover you can hide behind' 3; Grove 'Tall trees; hides wards' 4; meter '54 / 80 points'. §6.2: Pond 'Deep: only swimmers cross … 2 per tile | Tidehold, Verdant | Keeper 3'; Stream '1 per tile'; Cliff edge 'Free (made by height)', blocks climbing; Hedge '1 per tile', blocks, cut in 3 s; no Hill or Grove. §6.1 budgets: outer 30 + 15 × level (45-105), Heart 40 + 10 × Spire (100 at Spire 6).
rec: The tray (or the Terrain editor it opens) reads content/terrain.json; note in §23.5.
verdict_why: Confirmed. screens_main.js:157's terrain tray has these features: Pond 'Swimmers ignore; slows raiders.' 4 pts, Stream 6 pts, Hill 5 pts, Cliff 8 pts, Hedge 3 pts and Grove 4 pts, with a fixed meter of '54 / 80 points'. The §6.2 rows differ. Pond: 'Deep: only swimmers cross; everyone else goes round', 2 per tile, Tidehold and Verdant only, Keeper 3. Stream: 1 per tile. Cliff edge: 'Free (made by height)', blocks climbing. Hedge: 1 per tile, 'Blocks; cut through in 3 seconds'. Hill and Grove do not exist. §6.1's budgets are 30 + 15 a level for outer realms (45 to 105) and 40 + 10 per Spire level for the Heart (100 at Spire 6). No realm gives 80. §23.5 has no terrain row.

title: No law pylons in the realm view (must-show 'pylons'); §23.5 records only that pylons 'look alike'
evidence: realm_diorama.js contains no pylon object (searches for 'pylon'/'obelisk' find nothing; laws appear only as the LAWS slot strip, screens_main.js:338-341, markup 488-496). The tray's 'Pylon' places a spire-shaped building ('spire' glyph). §23.2 must-show 'pylons'; §10.2 'Law Pylon: One per law slot'; §21.5 'An obelisk topped with the school's shape'; §23.1 'law pylons with their zones. Law chips float over the pylons they belong to'. §23.5 row: 'Workers, pylons, wards and guard posts look alike'.
rec: Draw a Law Pylon per woven slot with school shape, zone ring and a floating chip; correct §23.5's row to say pylons are absent, not look-alike.
verdict_why: Confirmed. realm_diorama.js has no pylon or obelisk object; grep finds 0 matches for 'pylon'. Laws appear only as the realm's laws strip (screens_main.js:338-341) and as ambient effects (lawFX :1312, where Stillness draws a clock face round the Heart's Spire). Outer-realm layouts (GEN, :89) contain no law structure at all. The tray's 'Pylon' uses key 'spire', so placing one builds the BT 'Spire' building ('Holds the realm’s laws') and not a Law Pylon per slot. The document requires them: §10.2 'Law Pylon: One per law slot', §21.5 'An obelisk topped with the school's shape', §23.1 'law pylons with their zones. Law chips float over the pylons they belong to', and §23.2 lists pylons as a must-show. §23.5's row ('Workers, pylons, wards and guard posts look alike') assumes pylons are drawn. They are not, so the design gives no pylon to follow.
corrected: Correct as stated. Add that the tray's 'Pylon' builds the diorama's Spire building type, so a placed 'Pylon' looks like a second Spire. §23.5's realm-view row should say that per-slot law pylons are absent, not that they look like other buildings.

title: Round island with a circular tile mask against §5.2's square grids
evidence: realm_diorama.js:92 setTiles keeps tiles with hypot(x,z) ≤ 10.2·IK; :1057 grid drawn at opacity 0 except in place/move mode. §5.2 grids 10 by 10 … 14 by 14; client/ext/src/island.rs `side()` and sim/src/island.rs are square.
rec: Keep the round rock and draw §5.2's square grid inside it, faint always and strong in edit modes; note in §23.5.
verdict_why: Confirmed, and the finding understates it. realm_diorama.js:91-92 setTiles keeps only tiles with hypot(x+.5,z+.5) ≤ 10.2×IK. In realm view rebuild sets ik=2.05 (:1053), so the disc has a radius of about 21 tiles: roughly 1,370 tiles, about 42 across. It is the same in every realm at every level. canPlace (:1015) uses this set. The grid overlay is created at opacity 0 (:1062) and shows only in place and move modes (:1434). §5.2 gives grids of 10 by 10 at realm level 1 up to 14 by 14 at level 5, and §21.1 says 'A realm is 10 to 14 tiles across'. sim/src/island.rs and client/ext/src/island.rs use a square side. §23.5 has no row for this.
corrected: The realm view's placeable grid is a disc of radius 10.2 × 2.05, about 21 tiles (about 1,370 tiles, about 42 across). It is the same in every realm at every level (realm_diorama.js:92, :1053, :1015). §5.2 asks for a square grid of 10 by 10 to 14 by 14 by realm level, and §21.1 says a realm is 10 to 14 tiles across. The grid is drawn only in place and move modes (:1062, :1434). The round rock can stay as art around a square §5.2 grid.

title: The Heart shown as a Spirit realm with the Spire's level, and crown laws invisible on home and in the realm view
evidence: screens_main.js:35 `heart:{name:'The Heart',school:'Spirit',lv:6,slots:2,crown:2,crownLaws:['kinship'],laws:['stillness']}`; realm_diorama.js:61 heart school 'Spirit'; focus card 'Spirit · Level 6 · 1 of 2 law slots' with only Stillness (hrs/shots4/home_focus_heart.png); realm view shows a third 'Locked' slot on the Heart (realm_laws_open.png). §5.2 Heart 'Neutral | Circle | None'; §5.1 'A crown law works in every realm of its universe … The Heart has 2 realm slots'; §23.2 'Realms with their laws'.
rec: Neutral circle for the Heart; 'Spire N' instead of a realm level; crown laws on the Heart and shown in every realm's law strip; no locked third slot on the Heart.
verdict_why: Confirmed. screens_main.js:35 has heart {school:'Spirit', lv:6, slots:2, crown:2, crownLaws:['kinship'], laws:['stillness']}, and realm_diorama.js:61 also gives the Heart school 'Spirit'. The home focus card (capture home_focus_heart) reads 'Spirit · Level 6 · 1 of 2 law slots' and shows only Stillness. crownLaws is never read on home or in the realm view; grep finds it only at line 35, and crown slots are mentioned only on the Weaving screen (:373). The realm view always draws three law cells (screens_main.js:340, `[0,1,2]`), so the Heart shows a third 'LOCKED' slot (capture realm_laws_open). The document: §5.2 Heart 'Neutral | Circle | None'. §5.1 'A crown law works in every realm of its universe, including the Heart' and 'The Heart has 2 realm slots'. §23.2 must-show 'Realms with their laws'. A Spirit Heart would also change §5.2's 20% stability discount and 10% production bonus, which makes it a mechanic. Register G19 records that the Heart has no realm level, but only for ward and post counts, so it does not cover this.

title: A timer and a shield on the home screen
evidence: screens_main.markup.html:386: Defence side button carries a cyan shield chip '5h 12m' (hud_shield_10). The player is Keeper 24 with 128 heists (menu header, markup 446). §18.8 'No countdown pressure | No "last chance" banners, no timers on the home screen'; §12.3 'New players can't be raided by other players for their first 72 hours, or until they raid a player themselves'; §22.1 'Never sold … Shields or heist retries'. No other shield exists.
rec: No timer on home; show §12.3's protection only while it lasts, in words, on the defence screen; add the row to §23.5.

title: A curation law swap is instant and free, but §5.6 makes every law change a weave
