verdict_why: Confirmed. The design has a four-way facing dial and the message 'Post N now faces …' (screens_meta.js:552, 583), and every cone follows the chosen facing (cuEval 112-113). §13.3 and §23.2 list only 'move a post'. §12.17 says 'Patrols or holds its post'. §21.12 implies a guard has a facing but never says who sets it. The simulation posts every guard at 270° (sim/src/lib.rs:547), and Unaware guards keep that facing (1748-1752). The island bundle has no facing field. A facing changes what a guard sees, so under §23.5 the dial cannot be adopted until the document states it.

title: A curated defence's origin is undefined, and so is whether it must be in band to save
evidence: Design: SAVE refuses outside 30–45% ('Bring the hold inside 30–45% to save', screens_meta.js:558) and shows the authored band for the Heart. §13.2: generated islands are held to their realm level's band (25–40% at realm level 1); authored islands to 30–45%; 'Every island is tagged with its origin, so the matchmaker holds it to the right band (12.22)'. No section says what an edited generated defence becomes, or whether saving needs the band.
rec: Define a curated defence's origin. Example: it counts as generated while only §13.3's verbs were used, and as authored once terrain is edited. Also say whether a defence outside its band can be saved (with a warning or not at all).
verdict_why: Confirmed. The design refuses SAVE outside 30–45% ('Bring the hold inside 30–45% to save', screens_meta.js:558) and draws that band (570). §13.2 (7535) holds authored islands to 30–45%, generated islands to their realm level's band (25–40% at realm level 1), and tags every island with its origin. No section says which origin a curated generated defence has, or whether a defence must be inside its band to be saved. A save refusal is a player-visible rule, so a decision is needed. D62 covers only the Workshop publish check.

title: The hold figure on curation and the Workshop has no fast source
evidence: Design: a hold % recomputed instantly for every layout, swap, river choice, post move and BEST heat-map tile, from the formula base + 2·min(3, seen tiles) + a per-law bonus (screens_meta.js:105-125, 513-516); the Workshop's '38% held' gauge (markup 517). Doc: hold is a rate over 800+ raids (§13.2-13.4). §23.2 asks the preview to 're-generate fast enough not to break the flow' but gives no fast source for hold. D62 records that the Workshop cannot measure per publish.
rec: Decide the source. Option A: the live stealth-path count (§13.3's own measure, exact and instant) plus a measured hold from a server queue cached by island digest, shown as 'measuring…' until it lands. Option B: an on-device small batch with its error printed. The document should say a preview shows the counted measure and the measured hold, never an estimate shown as a measurement.
verdict_why: Confirmed. cuEval (screens_meta.js:105-125) computes hold as base + 2·min(3, seen tiles on each landing path) + a per-law bonus (+3 for rivers across). That figure is shown live on curation, and the Workshop shows '38% held · fair' (markup 517). The document defines hold as a rate measured over 800 or more raids (§13.3, §13.4). §23.2 asks only that the preview 're-generate fast enough not to break the flow' and names no fast source for hold. The design's figure is an invented estimate presented as a measurement. D62 records that the Workshop cannot measure hold per publish, but not the curation side.

title: Every guard's cone is drawn at once, with gradients
evidence: Curation and the terrain editor's SIGHT pass every post's cone to the view (screens_meta.js:520, 1031). The 3D view draws unselected cones at 14% opacity, with colour-gradient fans and soft tile textures (realm_diorama.js:384-409). §21.12 (11086-11088): 'One shape at a time. The selected guard's vision is drawn; the others show only their facing' and 'Sharp edges, no gradients'.
rec: Add a §23.5 row. The build draws one post's tiles with hard edges, as RealmView already does, and cycles between posts.
verdict_why: Confirmed. realm_diorama.js:384-391 draws every post's tiles: unselected at 0.14 opacity with the soft texture, plus a vertex-colour gradient fan for each post. Curation passes all cones (screens_meta.js:520). §21.12 (11086-11088) says 'The selected guard's vision is drawn; the others show only their facing' and 'Sharp edges, no gradients'. The build already follows §21.12 (client/scripts/realm_view.gd:7, 31, 244). Only a §23.5 row is missing.

title: Rule texts on the editing screens differ from the document's
evidence: Bell post: the design says 'Rings when passed / Guards within 4 tiles hear it / Held breath silences it'; §6.2 says 'Rings if bumped / Raises the realm's alarm one level (12.17) / Delay makes the ring come late'. Ruin wall's law line: 'Echoes bounce off it' against 'Shifting stones moves ruin walls too'. Five feature texts are shortened and four family names abbreviated (screens_meta.js:27-66 against content/terrain.json). On the curation cards, Sleepwalk and Glowing dark differ from §7.7 (3598, 2978) (js:26). Mangrove banks differs from §8.4 (js:9). The Loremaker rewards omit 'a say in one season's theme' (js:1146 against §18.7).
rec: Add one §23.5 row covering feature, law, resonance and ladder texts on the editing screens. The build reads all of these texts from content.
verdict_why: Confirmed, and the reader undercounted. Bell post: 'Rings when passed / Guards within 4 tiles hear it / Held breath silences it' against §6.2's 'Rings if bumped / Raises the realm's alarm one level (12.17) / Delay makes the ring come late', which is a different rule. Ruin wall: 'Echoes bounce off it' against 'Shifting stones moves ruin walls too'. Comparing against content/terrain.json, about fifteen of the 39 rows differ in substance, not five. Raised ground drops 'or a leap'. Stairs adds 'Noisy underfoot' where the document has '—'. Stream drops the Spores clause and Pond the Frictionless clause. Thicket changes 'linger longer' to 'linger'. Hot spring drops 'while standing in it'. The Sleepwalk and Glowing dark lines in CULAW differ from their sheets. The Loremaker rewards omit 'a say in one season's theme' (screens_meta.js:1146). The build reads texts from content, so this is a §23.5 completeness row.
corrected: About fifteen of the design's 39 terrain rows differ in substance from §6.2 (content/terrain.json), not five, including two that change a rule: Bell post (alarm level against hearing within 4 tiles; Delay against Held breath) and Stairs, whose 'Noisy underfoot' is a sight-column line the document does not have. Add the Sleepwalk and Glowing dark curation lines (§7.7), Mangrove banks (§8.4) and the Loremaker rewards (§18.7). The build reads all of these from content.

title: Moss is neither designed nor built
evidence: §6.1 (1164): every featureless tile is moss, and a Keeper clears it at 1 terrain point a tile. F29 was closed on this as the defender's answer to ambushes. Design: no moss and no clearing tool (screens_meta.js:27-104). Build: Island::empty lays plain ground (sim/src/island.rs:248-264); only fixtures place moss (750-762); the extension's bare ground is plain (client/ext/src/island.rs:130-151).
rec: The design adds a 'Clear moss' tool and draws moss as ground (§21.12). The simulation makes moss the default and charges a point for clearing it. Add a §23.5 row for the design omission.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §6.1 (1164): every featureless tile is raised with moss, and a Keeper clears it at 1 terrain point a tile. The register's note on F29 marks it fixed on exactly this quiet-surface rule. The design has no moss ground and no clear tool; 'moss' appears only in names and kinds. sim Island::empty lays Tile::default, which is plain (sim/src/island.rs:249-263). Only the fixtures place moss (750-762). The extension's set_ground writes Surface::Plain for bare ground (client/ext/src/island.rs:141-145). No register item records that the build lacks default moss. Moss decides whether an ambush can be reached, so this is a player-visible rule.

title: §13 calls geometry 'free, unlimited'; §6.1 gives it a budget
evidence: §13's layer table (7450): Geometry 'Free, unlimited'. §13.4 (7675): 'Geometry costs nothing and is unlimited'. §6.1 (1154): 30 terrain points plus 15 per realm level for an outer realm, 40 plus 10 per Spire level for the Heart, 'it's the budget that limits it'. §5.2's table has a terrain points column. The terrain editor's points bar exists to show that budget.
rec: Reword §13 and §13.4: 'Geometry costs nothing to change and is limited only by terrain points (6.1)'.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §13's layer table (7450) gives Geometry 'Free, unlimited', and §13.4 (7675) says 'Geometry costs nothing and is unlimited'. Against that, §6.1 (1154) gives a terrain budget ('it's the budget that limits it'), §9.5 (4582) says 'Free; limited by terrain points (6.1)', and §5.2 has a terrain points row (711). F16 quotes 'free, unlimited' but does not raise the contradiction.

title: The Heart's terrain budget needs the Spire level, and the sandbox's budget is unstated
evidence: The Heart's budget depends on the Spire level, which no island bundle carries, so Island::check cannot hold it alone. Today nothing counts terrain points: not sim/src/island.rs:144-169, not the extension's budget() (client/ext/src/island.rs:207-223), not the server (server/src/universe.mjs:287). §18.6 lifts the stability limit in the Workshop sandbox and says nothing about terrain points.
rec: The document says whether the Workshop sandbox keeps §6.1's budget, and at which realm level. The build adds a TooMuchTerrain problem, with the server passing in the budget (Spire level for the Heart).
verdict_why: Confirmed. §6.1 sets the Heart's budget at 40 + 10 per Spire level, and the bundle carries no Spire level. The Problem enum in sim/src/island.rs:143-169 has no terrain check. The extension's budget() (client/ext/src/island.rs:207-219) counts only wards, guards and laws. Server problems() (universe.mjs:280-290) checks realm and Vault level only. §18.6 lifts the stability limit in the sandbox and says nothing about terrain points. G19 is the related item for wards and posts in the Heart.

title: No rule for placing directional and two-ended terrain features
evidence: These features need a direction or a second point: ramp and stairs (which way is up), rapids ('pushes anyone 1 tile a second downstream'), waterfall (which side the ledge is on), tunnel ('joining two points up to 6 tiles apart'). The design places any feature with a single tap and no direction (screens_meta.js:98). §6.2 gives the effects but no owner choice; §7.10's placement rule covers laws, not terrain.
rec: State that the owner sets the direction and the tunnel's two ends, and give the generator's rule for each. The bundle carries them, which is a rules-version change (§24.11).
verdict_why: Confirmed. §6.2 gives Tunnel 'joining two points up to 6 tiles apart' (1227), Rapids 'pushes … downstream' (1285), and Waterfall and Ramp/Stairs effects, but no owner choice of direction or ends. §6.2's Chute row (796-798) does say 'The owner sets the direction', which shows the document states this where it means it. The design places with a single tap and no direction (screens_meta.js:98). F12 covers the eight laws, not terrain features.

title: 'A person reviews it within an hour' before a Workshop island goes live
evidence: Design: the publish celebration says 'A person reviews it within an hour. Then anyone can raid it…' (markup 542), and the draft is tagged 'IN REVIEW · 1 H' (screens_meta.js:1161). Doc: §18.6 (9070) 'featured islands are reviewed by a person'; §24's Workshop row 'scanned automatically'; §20.4: a part-time moderator reviews reports within 24 h. The server publishes at once (server/src/workshop.mjs publish). This is a staffing promise the document never makes, and it changes when an island becomes playable.
rec: Add a §23.5 row: an island goes live when it passes the checks, and 'in review' applies only to the spotlight.
verdict_why: Confirmed. Markup 542 reads 'A person reviews it within an hour. Then anyone can raid it…' and the draft tag reads 'IN REVIEW · 1 H' (screens_meta.js:1161). The document has a person review featured islands (§18.6, 9072), reports within 24 h (§20.4, 10227), and published islands 'scanned automatically' (§24, 11682). Nothing holds an island back for human review. The server publishes at once (server/src/workshop.mjs:104-150). The design adds both a delay before an island is playable and a staffing promise.

title: The design has no Remix or Withdraw, though a launch gate depends on remix
evidence: §25.1 (12131): '10% have remixed one'. §27.5 (13085): 'one-tap "remix this island"'. §20.12: islands can be withdrawn at the player's request. Design: island sheets offer only Report and Play, or Edit and Share for one's own (screens_meta.js:1153-1154). The build already has both (client/features/workshop/workshop_controller.gd:153, 166; server/src/workshop.mjs:160, 381).
rec: The design adds Remix to every island sheet and Withdraw to the player's own. The build keeps both.
verdict_why: Remix is confirmed. §25.1 (12131) sets a 10% remix gate and §27.5 (13085) promises a one-tap 'remix this island', but the design's sheets offer only Report/Play or Edit/Share (screens_meta.js:1153-1154). Withdraw is mis-cited: §20.12's 'withdrawn entirely at the player's request' is about an account being deleted. A general withdraw is the build's own reading. The build already has both (workshop_controller.gd:153, 166; workshop.mjs:158, 381), and remix is not on §23.2's Workshop must-show. The only gap is a button the design lacks, so minor.
corrected: The design has no Remix, which §27.5's one-tap 'remix this island' and §25.1's 10% gate require; the build already has it. §20.12's withdrawal at the player's request applies when an account is deleted. A general Withdraw on one's own island is the build's reading, needed to free one of §20.12's limited slots, and the design has none.

title: Unstated whether a Workshop island is one realm or several
evidence: Design: a draft of '2 realms' and Glass Maze '1 realm' (screens_meta.js:1163, 1172). §18.6: 'an island is a set of laws, terrain, guards and a layout', with nothing on realms. The server stores one bundle with one realm level (server/src/workshop.mjs:146-149).
rec: State whether a Workshop island is one realm or a small universe. A universe would need crossing realms in the simulation.
verdict_why: Confirmed. The design shows a '2 realms' draft and 'Glass Maze · 1 realm' (screens_meta.js:1163, 1172). §18.6 says only 'an island is a set of laws, terrain, guards and a layout'. The server stores one bundle with one realm_level (workshop.mjs:146-149). D71, which keeps a heist to one island, is related but does not ask the Workshop question.

title: The Workshop claims 'under 20% escape and players rate it unfair'
evidence: Design: 'If the escape rate falls under 20%, players start rating it unfair' (screens_meta.js:1153), shown on islands escaping 18–61%. The document has no such figure; published islands are checked to hold 30–45% (§18.7, §13.2). §23.5's Workshop checklist row covers the 62% check, not this sentence.
rec: Drop the sentence or give it a source under §19.22's rules. Show each island's measured escape rate.
verdict_why: Confirmed. The footer of the player's own island sheet reads 'If the escape rate falls under 20%, players start rating it unfair' (screens_meta.js:1153). The document has no such figure: authored islands are held to 30–45% (§13.2, §18.7). §23.5's Workshop checklist row covers the '62% · Lv 6 band' check, not this sentence. It is an unsourced claim in player-facing text.

title: The defender's report has four measures, none defined for one raid or recorded by the simulation
evidence: §13.2 (7581) and §23.2 (11269): 'the haul denied, how long the defence held, where the crew was seen, what fired'. §13.4 defines haul denied over many raids against a no-defence baseline, not for one raid; 'held the crew up' has no measure. sim Outcome (sim/src/heist.rs:146-167) records none of the four. §24's validation is sampled, so most raids are never re-simulated on the server.
rec: Define each measure for a single raid. Examples: denied = what the crew could carry from the exposed Vault less what it banked; held = seconds from landing to escape or capture; seen = tiles where a guard reached Alerted, named by the nearest building; fired = wards triggered, bells rung, the guardian Sage's power. The build records these in sim/ and computes the report by re-simulating when the defender opens it.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §13.2 (7581) and §23.2 (11269) require each raid's report to show the haul denied, how long the defence held, where the crew was seen and what fired. §13.4 (7679) defines haul denied as an expectation over many raids against a no-defence baseline, which is not a single-raid figure. 'How long it held the crew up' has no measure. sim Outcome (sim/src/heist.rs:147-167) records grade, banked, capacity, caught, out, pages, cracked and left: no time held, no sighting tiles, no list of what fired. §24 (11700) says server validation is sampled.

title: The defence log shows a raid while it is happening
evidence: Design: 'A crew is in Tidehold now · The raider's name shows when the raid ends' (markup 232). §13: 'The defender is notified afterwards and can watch the replay'; watching live is version 1.1 (7480-7482); §17.8: 'raids are anonymous while they happen'. Showing a raid in progress changes what a player can see.
rec: Drop the banner at launch, or add to §13: 'a defender sees that a raid is under way in a realm, never who or how'.
verdict_why: Confirmed. Markup 232 reads 'A crew is in Tidehold now · The raider's name shows when the raid ends'. §13 (7467) says 'The defender is notified afterwards', and watching live is version 1.1 (7480-7482). §17.8's 'anonymous while they happen' is consistent with hiding the name, but not with notifying the defender mid-raid. The banner changes what a player sees. The snapshot rule means the defender cannot act on it, so the impact is small.

title: The three rehearsal crews have names but no behaviour
evidence: §13 (7479) names the crews 'cautious, greedy or fast' and gives no policy. The harness has other crews (Careless/Competent/Optimal/Clearing, tools/heist_harness/policy.py:460-534). D66 asks for the reference crews to move into the simulation. The design gives each crew one line ('Waits for gaps, never runs', 'Loads until the bag is full', 'Runs the shortest route'; screens_meta.js:590).
rec: §13 gives each crew its rule in one sentence: when it moves, when it stops loading, how it picks a route. The build writes the three in sim/ alongside D66's port.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §13 (7479) names the rehearsal crews 'cautious, greedy or fast' and gives no policy. The harness has Careless/Competent/Optimal/Clearing (tools/heist_harness/policy.py:460-555), and nothing in sim/, server/ or client/ implements cautious, greedy or fast. The design gives one line each (screens_meta.js:590). D66 covers porting the reference crews into the simulation, not defining these three.

title: The owner's answers F39, C41, F44, F46 and F51 are not in v3.6, and Screens v3 draws the rules they replaced
evidence: docs/decisions/answers.json: F39 B, C41 B, F44 D, F46 B ('client: the target card shows laws, guards and ward counts'), F51 B, all 'build: done'; server follows them (server/src/economy.mjs:163-178; service.mjs:532). v3.6 still says 'Entry fee: 2% of the raider's Starlight, from 100 to 25,000, returned in full after a clean heist' (§9.4 line 4560), 'within 3 Keeper levels' (§12.3 line 6922), the paid scout (§12.4 line 6936), and its new §23.2 Observatory row says 'showing only the free scouting facts (12.4)' (line 11237); diffs.txt shows none of §5.4/9.4/12.3/12.4/12.22 changed. Design: fee from holdings on every card (data_v35.js:15), 'Keepers 21–27' (screens_main.js:524), locked 'Laws, guards and wards show after a scout' and 'Scout · 100 Aether' (screens_main.markup.html:649-652).
rec: Owner confirms whether the answers stand. If they do, apply the brief's drafted doc_edit text in v3.7 and reword §23.2's Observatory row to the free facts the answer makes free; the Observatory, scout and planner then draw the fee per target from the server and no scout paywall. If v3.6 is meant to reverse them, record the reversals and revert the server.
verdict_why: Confirmed in part. The answers file (docs/decisions/answers.json) records F39 B, C41 B, F44 D, F46 B and F51 B, each marked build: done. The server follows them: server/src/economy.mjs:156-178 takes the fee as 2% of B(V) and returns it after clean or loud heists and half after a partial one, and tools/design_facts.py:235 sets the Keeper window to two below and three above. v3.6 did not change §5.4, §9.4, §12.3, §12.4 or §12.22. It still says 'Entry fee: 2% of the raider's Starlight, from 100 to 25,000' (line 4560), 'within 3 Keeper levels' (line 6922) and the paid scout (line 6936). The §23.2 Observatory row v3.6 rewrote (line 11237) says 'showing only the free scouting facts (12.4)', which assumes the paid scout that F46 B removed. Screens v3 draws the document's rules: the fee from holdings (data_v35.js:15), 'Keepers 21–27' (screens_main.js:524), and the locked 'Laws, guards and wards show after a scout' with 'Scout · N Aether' (screens_main.markup.html:649, screens_main.js:524). Two parts are wrong. For C41 the design already draws the answer: its outcome table (data_v35.js:14) gives the fee back after Loud, half after Partial, and to the defender after Foiled, which is §12.9's column and so C41 B. For F51 nothing in these screens contradicts the answer. What is new beyond the open register items: v3.6's rewritten §23.2 row still assumes the paid scout, and the client must choose between the server (the answers) and both the document and Screens v3.
corrected: v3.6 does not carry the owner's answers on F39 (fee keyed to B(V)), F44 (window from two below to three above) and F46 (free scouting), and its rewritten §23.2 Observatory row still assumes §12.4's paid scout. Screens v3 draws the pre-answer rules: the fee as 2% of holdings, Keepers ±3 and a locked paid scout. The server follows the answers. The design's fee-return table already matches C41 B (§12.9's column), and nothing in these screens bears on F51. Owner to confirm that the answers stand, so v3.7 applies them and the client draws the per-target fee from the server with no scout lock.
existing: F39, F44, F46 (also C41, F51). All are open, with drafted document edits that v3.6 did not apply.

title: The scout report shows guard posts, ward positions and patrol routes
evidence: §12.4 line 6936 'how many wards of each type it has, but not where they are'; §12.12 line 7141 'A scout shows no positions (12.4); patrols are learned in the heist'; C37 fixed by brief 38 (tools/audit_register.py:7430-7434). Design: realm_diorama.js:267-276 draws red reach discs and ×N pins on every guard post and rings with ✦ pins on wards; screens_main.js:532 and 537-540 hold patrol prose ('Two loops around the Spire; the Breaker holds the vault door', 'The Breaker guards the vault; Wardens loop the Spire') and post/ward coordinates; Threats tab reads '5 wards · 3 hidden traps'. §23.5 lists only the Heart's Land here flag for this screen (line 11485).
rec: Add a §23.5 row: 'Scout report | Guard posts, ward rings and patrol notes in the 3D view | No positions and no patrols | 12.4, 12.12'. Build the scout view from counts only (RulebornIsland.scouting()).
verdict_why: Confirmed. §12.4 (line 6936) says a scout shows wards 'but not where they are', and §12.12 (line 7141) says 'A scout shows no positions (12.4); patrols are learned in the heist'. Register item C37 recorded this as decided by brief 38. The design's buildScout (realm_diorama.js:267-276) draws a red reach disc and a ×N pin on every guard post, and a ring with a ✦ pin on every ward. The scout data holds patrol prose and post and ward coordinates (screens_main.js:532, 537-540). My render of the Threats tab (oslp_shots/scout_heart_threats.png) shows the ×2 guard pins, the ward rings, 'The Breaker guards the vault; Wardens loop the Spire.' and '5 wards · 3 hidden traps'. The only scout-report row in §23.5 is the Land here flag on the Heart (line 11486). Showing positions changes what a player can see, so under §23.5 it is a mechanic a design may not add.
existing: C37 covers the rule, which is already decided; the design's deviation from it is not registered.

title: What of a target's layout the raider sees before the heist is unwritten
evidence: §5.4 lines 822-825: land on any edge tile, heard 'unless the spot is in fog, darkness or tall grass', so the raider must see edge terrain to choose; §12.12 line 7141 'A scout shows no positions'; §10.3 marks Crystal Wall and Thorn Hedge 'Seen: Always' (in the heist); §11.8 line 6229 the Cartographer sells a map 'with ward positions'; F46 notes the bundle is public. The design's scout and planner show the whole realm in 3D with buildings, the Vault and a route to it (realm_diorama.js:255-266).
rec: One sentence in §12.4: before the heist the game draws each realm's ground and terrain, the Vault and the always-seen wards, and no guard posts, hidden wards or pylons (unless the Cartographer's map is held).
verdict_why: Confirmed as a gap. §12.4 lists the free facts and the scout facts and says nothing about the target's ground, terrain, buildings or Vault position. §12.12 says only 'A scout shows no positions'. The document still needs the raider to see some of the layout before the heist. §5.4 makes a landing heard 'unless the spot is in fog, darkness or tall grass'. §23.2's Landing picker row (line 11293) asks for 'Every outer realm's edge, what guards would hear'. Showing whether a spot would be heard (guards within 6 tiles) itself reveals where guards stand, against 'no positions'. The design shows the whole realm in 3D, with the Vault beam and a route (realm_diorama.js:255-266). No register item says what is drawn before the heist. F46 says only that the bundle is public and the client still hides ward positions. G40 covers the landing details.
existing: None covers this. Related: F46, C37, G40.

title: Generated fallback targets have no label in the Observatory
evidence: §12.22 step 4 line 7433: 'Each is labelled as a generated target at the point of attack, because it is nobody's realm and must not pass as another player's'; empty band's fallbacks 'labelled with the band they come from'. Design has no generated state and its final ribbon code labels anything not a Trace 'ECHO' (screens_main.js:525: tag:tg.traceOn?'TRACE · 24 H':'ECHO').
rec: §23.5 row; the build carries a generated flag (and band) in the Observatory list and draws a GENERATED ribbon and reason.
verdict_why: The rule is confirmed. §12.22 step 4 says a fallback target 'is labelled as a generated target at the point of attack ... must not pass as another player's', and an empty band's fallbacks are labelled 'with the band they come from'. Screens v3 has no state for a generated target. One part is mis-stated: the ribbon does not label every non-Trace target ECHO. It is drawn only when hasTag:!!(tg.traceOn||tg.echo) (screens_main.js:524), so a generated target would carry no ribbon at all. The design is missing a state rather than showing something wrong, and the build has to add it. D66 records that the server does not build generated fallbacks yet.
corrected: Screens v3 has no state for a §12.22 generated fallback target. Its ribbon is drawn only for a Trace or an echo (hasTag, screens_main.js:524), so a generated target would carry no label. The build must add a 'Generated' label, with the source band when the band was empty, wherever §12.22's 'point of attack' is.
existing: D66 covers the server not building generated fallbacks. The missing label is not registered.

title: Drifting ruins: three ruins at one difficulty each, or three ruins with three difficulties each
evidence: §12.10 line 7115 'three universes built by the game each day'; §12.12 line 7135 'Every ruin offers three openly labelled difficulties with their rewards shown, and a recommendation the player can ignore'; §23.2 line 11237 'drifting ruins apart, at three labelled difficulties (12.12)'. Design: three tiles Easy/Slow rivers, Medium/Glass, Hard/Haste, no rewards per difficulty, no recommendation, each straight to the planner (screens_main.js:526).
rec: Decide and say it once. By §12.12's rule text: each of the three ruins opens to its three difficulties with rewards and a 'Suggested' one; reword §23.2 to match and add the design's reading to §23.5 as a difference.

title: The planner refuses to start without a Carrier, and starts with fewer than three
evidence: §11.1 lines 5922-5968: every role carries (Scout 104, Breaker 104, Carrier 160/300, Warden 138, Mender 104) 'so no one bag decides the haul'; §12.5 line 6950 'A crew of 3 to 5', no role requirement. verdict_why: Confirmed. pWarn says 'No Carrier: nobody can carry loot out' (screens_main.js:584). title: Forms album's USE THIS LOOK re-skins a ruleborn after hatching
evidence: screens_meta.js:1204-1205: actT 'USE THIS LOOK', toast '<note> <kind> is now its look'. §11.10: the form is set by the Nursery's laws at hatching and changes the look and one quirk; nothing changes it later. A look apart from its quirk would mislead a raider reading a guard.
rec: Drop it (build 'Show mine' instead) or write a rule in §11.10 first.
verdict_why: The design part is confirmed. js:1204-1205 shows 'USE THIS LOOK' with the toast '<note> <kind> is now its look'. The finding's reading of the document is not. §11.10 does not say that nothing changes a form later; it is silent. The design does not say whether the action changes owned ruleborn in heists and on guard or only the album and portrait display. The concern still stands. A form's look signals its quirk (§11.10 table), so a look applied apart from the hatched form would change what a raider sees of a guard. §23.5 forbids building anything like that until it is written. As a display-only choice it would break no rule.
corrected: §11.10 is silent on changing a form after hatching. Screens v3's USE THIS LOOK (js:1204-1205) is unspecified in scope. If it changes a ruleborn's look in heists or on guard, it alters what raiders see (the look signals the quirk), and §23.5 bars building it until a rule is written. title: A Sage level may shorten 'the one 20-second cooldown'
evidence: §11.7 (:6217): 'Every fifth level improves one power (an extra use, a longer effect or a shorter cooldown)' and, after it, every Sage follows 'the one 20-second cooldown'.

evidence: §11.4 (:6147-6153): '+8% health and power, +5% carry' a level (compounding or additive: ×1.999 or ×1.72 at level 10) and 'abilities improve at levels 4, 7 and 10 (20% stronger effect each time)' without naming the parameter for abilities with two (Lantern Wisp 6 tiles and 6 s; Featherkin 3 tiles and one height level; Echoplate 8 s and 40%). The compounding half is already read one way by the repository: tools/decision_support.py:298 sets LEVEL_GROWTH = 1.08 and uses 1.08**(level−1), and docs/design/spec/vault.md:207 says 'crew power compounds at 1.08'. That half needs only a confirming sentence. The ability-parameter half is an open decision for the simulation and the Character screen's next-level numbers.
corrected: §11.4 does not say that +8%/+5% compounds. The repository already assumes it does (tools/decision_support.py:298), so this needs one confirming sentence. The open decision is which parameter of each multi-parameter ability grows 20% at levels 4, 7 and 10.

title: Where a ruleborn lives decides its ceiling and rest, and the Spire's places have no Hearth
evidence: §11.4: 'Highest level = 2 × the level of the Hearth the character lives in'; §11.6: 'Hearths shorten rest 5% per level'; §11.5: 'The roster holds 3 characters for the Spire plus the places in every Hearth'. The Spire's three have no Hearth level; nothing says how a character gets or changes its home. Related: F56 (starting universe).
rec: State the Spire places' ceiling and rest, and the housing rule.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §11.4 (:6153) says 'Highest level = 2 × the level of the Hearth the character lives in'. §11.6 says 'Hearths shorten rest 5% per level', and §10.2's Hearth rows (:5377-5405) give the ceilings and rest cuts per level. §11.5 (:6163) says '3 characters for the Spire plus the places in every Hearth'. Nothing gives the Spire's three a ceiling or a rest cut, and nothing says how a character is housed in or moved between Hearths (one per realm). F56 covers the starting universe, not housing. F1 and Q1 count Hearth homes but do not raise this.
corrected: As stated.

title: One-tap reassign needs a default slot, and the model's staffing order is unstated
evidence: §23.2 Roster must-show 'one-tap reassign'; §9.2: 'choosing which producer goes short is the decision'; open G22: §14.1 names no staffing order though the regenerated tables move by months with it. The design always assigns to a Star Well (screens_meta.js:196).
rec: One rule for both: the default tap follows the staffing order the published pacing assumes (extend G22).
verdict_why: Partly confirmed. §23.2's Roster row (:11243-11245) asks for 'one-tap reassign' and leaves the destination undefined. The design's Assign always sends to 'Star Well' (js:197, cited as 196), and it takes two taps (select, then Assign). Tying the default to G22's open staffing order is a reasonable extension rather than a separate document gap. The design's fixed Star Well breaks no stated rule, so this is a build need more than a deviation.
corrected: The single-tap destination of §23.2's 'one-tap reassign' is undefined, and the design always assigns to a Star Well in two taps (js:197). Use the staffing order G22 asks §14.1 to state as the default slot.

title: Rest modifiers combine by no stated rule, and 'success' for Loyal is undefined
evidence: §11.6 Hearths −5% a level; §11.3 Loyal 'rests 25% less after a success', Sleepy 'rests 50% longer'; §12.9's 45/60/180 by outcome. Order of application and whether Loud or Partial count as a success are not stated; the Roster's rest timers and the server's settlement need them.
rec: State the order (e.g. multiplicative) and which outcomes are a success.
verdict_why: Half confirmed. The order in which §11.6 Hearth −5%/level, §11.3 Loyal −25% and Sleepy +50% combine on §12.9's 45/60/180 is not stated. The claim that 'success' is undefined is weak. §9.6 (:4707) reads success as clean, loud or partial ('62.5% success times a 35/40/25 split of clean, loud and partial'), and §14.2 (:7740) contrasts successful heists with foiled ones. So success means any outcome but Foiled. The only open edge is a member caught in a Partial.
corrected: The document reads success as any outcome but Foiled (§9.6 :4707, §14.2 :7740). What is unstated is how the Hearth, Loyal and Sleepy modifiers combine (multiplicative or additive, in which order), and whether Loyal applies to a member caught in a Partial.

title: Naming a ruleborn is offered and unspecified
evidence: §19.20 (:9922): 'Naming a ruleborn is offered the first time one hatches, and a free outfit comes with it'. Nothing says typed or word-list for 13 to 15 (§20.7 keeps what others see to word lists), whether a name can change, or who sees it. The design shows names (Pip, Mo…) and no naming.
rec: State the naming rule alongside §20.7.
verdict_why: Confirmed, and stronger than claimed. §19.20 (:9922) offers naming at the first hatch, and nothing specifies it. §20.7 (:10249ff) restricts only island names to word lists for players aged 13 to 15. §24's security row (:11885) says the game has 'no free text', which a typed ruleborn name would contradict. Screens v3 shows names (js:191) and no naming flow.
corrected: As stated. In addition, §24 (:11885) says 'no free text', so a typed name contradicts it unless names come from word lists.

title: 'Crew' names two things: the heist crew and the 4-8-player group
evidence: §12.5 crew of 3-5 ruleborn; §17.7 (:8957) 'Crew | 4 to 8 | The people you actually play with'. The design's tab 'CREW' opens the Roster (markup 41-48); the server's /v1/crews and crews table are player groups (server/src/db.mjs:389-400).
rec: Label the tab 'Roster' (code uses roster), or rename one term in the document.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §12.5's crew is the 3 to 5 ruleborn on a heist. §17.7 (:8957) defines 'Crew | 4 to 8 | The people you actually play with'. The server implements the second meaning (server/src/db.mjs:389-400; /v1/crews in http.mjs:64-67). Screens v3's tab labelled 'Crew' opens the Roster hub (Gameplay_10_Roster.txt 'CREW' active; markup tabs.crewL). The register has no item.
corrected: As stated.

title: Sage hall: no levelling, an unassigned Sage shown 'resting', a heist Sage before Keeper 2
evidence: Sage hall shows 'Level 4 / 40 · levels with Insight' but no Insight, price or level-up (must-show 'levels'); bar fill level × 10% (screens_meta.js:364); unassigned Sage tagged 'RESTING' (js:359, 361) though Sages have no rest; the Archivist offered as heist Sage at Keeper 1 vs §12.5 'Sage: One, from Keeper level 2'; 'SAGES 2 / 6' counts two post-launch Sages vs §26.1's four at launch.
rec: Build per the report's section 4.8: Insight line and level-up once finding I is answered, 'Not chosen' wording, Keeper 2 gate with its reason, count over released Sages.
verdict_why: Partly real. The hall shows 'Level 4 / 40 · levels with Insight' and has no Insight balance, price or level-up control (§11.7, §9.5), and its bar fills level × 10% (js:364). The other parts are refuted or taste. The design is fixed at Keeper level 9 (js:280, KLV = 9), so it never offers a heist Sage at Keeper 1. The 'RESTING' tag (js:359) cannot be reached in the prototype, because the two unlocked Sages always hold the two roles (heistSage 0, guardSage 1, and setHeist/setGuard swap them), though the word would be wrong if copied. 'SAGES 2 / 6' with two 'A later season' silhouettes teases future content and breaks no rule.
corrected: The Sage hall shows a level but no Insight, price or level-up (§11.7, §9.5), and its bar fills level × 10% of a 40-level scale (js:364). Do not copy the 'RESTING' wording for an unassigned Sage (js:359). The Keeper-2 and '2 / 6' points do not stand: the design is at Keeper 9 (js:280), and the count is a display choice.

title: The guardian with only one Sage, and where a Sage's at-home effect applies
evidence: §11.7 (:6190): 'brings one Sage on each heist, and can station another at the Heart as its guardian' — whether the only Sage (Keeper 2 to 6) may guard instead; the 'At home' column's passives (Lab 20% faster, buildings 10% cheaper, Gardens 15% more, one more Observatory target) may apply always, only while home, or only as guardian. The design files at-home under 'On guard' (screens_meta.js:349).
rec: State both.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §11.7 (:6190) says 'brings one Sage on each heist, and can station another at the Heart as its guardian'. The Archivist is the only Sage until Keeper 7, and §12.5 and §14.2 (:7768) make heist Sages start at Keeper 2, so whether the lone Sage may guard is unstated. §11.7's 'At home' column mixes a passive (Lab 20% faster, buildings 10% cheaper, Gardens 15% more, one more Observatory target) with 'On guard'. Nothing says whether the passive needs the Sage to be home or to be the guardian. The design attaches 'At home' to the Guard card (js:349). docs/design/spec/response.md covers the on-guard power only.
corrected: As stated.

title: Forms album omits the skiff sail and quirks, uses colour-only pips; a stray's form is unstated
evidence: §11.10: 'completing one note across every kind unlocks a skiff sail' — not drawn; quirks (Hush noticed 10% later, Spark +5% power, Echo returns once at 20%) not shown; note pips coloured dots without symbols (screens_meta.js:1212) and roster state dots colour only (js:233) vs §20.8 'every note a symbol', 'no information carried by colour alone'. §11.9: strays are 'born under one of the laws the crew crossed' without a form rule when that law carries none of Hush, Spark, Echo.
rec: Draw the sail and quirks, add symbols and state icons; state a stray's form.
verdict_why: Mostly confirmed. Screens v3's forms code has no skiff sail or quirk text (no 'sail' or 'quirk' in js:1179-1217), against §11.10. The form pips (js:1214) have no note symbol, against §20.8's 'every note a symbol'. They do not carry the information by colour alone, though: their order is fixed (Hush, Spark, Echo) and filled and empty pips differ in brightness. The roster's state dot (js:234, cited as 233) separates idle, working and guarding by colour only, against §20.8's 'no information carried by colour alone'. A stray's form is unstated. §11.9 says strays are 'born under one of the laws the crew crossed', but §11.10's rule is decided by a Nursery's realm and its tie odds are 'shown before hatching', and neither applies to a stray.
corrected: The album omits the skiff sail (§11.10) and the quirks. Its pips lack note symbols (§20.8), though they do not rest on colour alone. The roster's state dot does (js:234). A stray's form is unstated (§11.9, §11.10).

title: The Starpass buys progress: +20% season stars and a Starpass-only quest
evidence: Design: '+20% ★' on the tier strip when the pass is owned (screens_meta.js:670 boostOn; markup 264) and every quest paying ×1.2 with it (screens_meta.js:684 "rT: '+' + (sPrem ? Math.round(q.r * 1.2) : q.r)"); daily quest 'Starpass: win a heist unseen' with prem: 1 (screens_meta.js:4), locked behind a STARPASS button (season_quests.png). Doc §18.8 (v3.6): 'The premium track sells looks and nothing else (22.1)'; §20.3: 'No power, speed or skipped waiting for money'; §14.8: 'no purchase ever fills one'. More stars buy free-track tiers that pay Essence and pages (§18.2).
rec: Build neither: quests pay the same with or without the pass, and no quest is reserved to pass holders.
verdict_why: Confirmed. Markup line 264 shows '+20% ★' when se.boostOn, which is set to sPrem (screens_meta.js:670). screens_meta.js:684 shows quest rewards as Math.round(q.r*1.2) with the pass. Quest d4 'Starpass: win a heist unseen' has prem:1 (screens_meta.js:4) and is locked behind a STARPASS button (season_quests_full.txt). This breaks §18.8 ('The premium track sells looks and nothing else'), §20.3 ('No power, speed or skipped waiting for money') and §14.8 ('no purchase ever fills one'). Neither §23.5 nor the register lists it. The build has no boost or quests (server/src, client/scripts). Downgraded from blocking: §23.5 already makes the document win, and the build does not do this.
corrected: Screens v3 promises a paid boost on the Season screen: '+20% ★' on the tier strip, quest rewards shown ×1.2 with the Starpass, and a daily quest reserved for pass holders. The prototype's own seQClaim (screens_meta.js:160) still adds the base q.r, so the error is in what the screen promises, not in what the prototype pays. The build must show the same rewards with or without the pass and reserve no quest for pass holders (§18.8, §20.3, §14.8).

title: Quests are not §14.6's daily goals, and season and event quests are new earnings
evidence: Design: four fixed daily quests with one free swap a day, four season quests (+120 to +200 stars) and two time-limited event quests ('Event · The Still Hour · 4 days', +300/+400) (screens_meta.js:2–5, 164–165; markup 277; season_quests_bottom.png). Doc §14.6: 'the player picks 3 of 6 offered goals … with one free swap. Rewards are small and shown as progress toward something the player chose.' §9.1/§18.2 list star sources; v3.6 defines no season or event quests; §18.8 'Nothing expires forever'.
rec: Build §14.6 (offer six, pick three, one swap, small rewards, daily cap per §20.3). Season and event quests only after they are written into §14.6/§18 with their rewards and caps.
verdict_why: Confirmed in screens_meta.js:2-5 and QS at :635: Daily (4 fixed quests, one of them pass-only, one free swap per seSwap), Season (4 quests, +120 to +200) and 'Event · The Still Hour · 4 days' (+400/+300). §14.6 says 'the player picks 3 of 6 offered goals ... with one free swap'. §9.1 lists 'goals' as a star source, but no section defines season or event goals. Season and event quests change what a player earns, and §23.5 says a design cannot add that. Citing §18.8's 'Nothing expires forever' is a stretch: that row is about unclaimed tiers.
corrected: Screens v3 replaces §14.6's 'pick 3 of 6, one free swap' with four fixed daily quests plus one swap. It also adds four season-long quests and two four-day event quests that pay season stars. §9.1 counts 'goals' as a star source, but only §14.6's daily goals are defined. Season and event quests are new earnings and need writing into §14.6 or §18 with their rewards and caps first.

title: The weekly streak pays a non-cosmetic reward, needs ten minutes a day, and shows no saver or repair
evidence: Design: seventh cell '+100' chest (screens_meta.js:683); 'Today · 6 of 10 min' (markup 276). Doc §14.6: 'playing on 4 days out of 7 keeps it going. One automatic saver a week covers a missed week, and a broken streak is repaired by playing two days in a row. Streak rewards are cosmetic.' §19.12 refuses obligation.
rec: Any play counts as a day; show the saver and the repair; the streak reward is a cosmetic.
verdict_why: Confirmed at screens_meta.js:683 (seventh cell '+100' chest) and markup line 276 ('Weekly streak · 4 of 7 days', 'Today · 6 of 10 min'). §14.6 says 'Streak rewards are cosmetic'. It also gives an automatic saver and a two-day repair, and the design draws neither. The +100 has no unit; stars are inferred from the Quests tab. The '6 of 10 min' bar implies a 10-minute daily threshold that §14.6, which counts any play on 4 of 7 days, does not have. No register item, nothing in the build.
corrected: The weekly streak card's '4 of 7 days' matches §14.6. Three things do not. Its reward is a number ('+100', most likely stars), where §14.6 says streak rewards are cosmetic. A 'Today 6 of 10 min' bar implies a minimum play time per day. The saver and the repair are not shown.

title: The era is drawn as a chapter of the season track; this week's era (a Season must-show) is missing
evidence: Design: gates 'ERA II · THE STILL HOUR' and 'ERA III' before tiers 11 and 21 (screens_meta.js:628; markup 267); event quests named after 'The Still Hour'. Doc §18.3: 'Each week one rule changes for every universe' (Heavy Stars … Quiet Week). §23.2 Season: 'League, track, era, weekly streak'. The server already serves GET /v1/era (server/src/http.mjs:10); icons_rbi.js has an unused season.era icon.
rec: Show the week's era, its rule in words and when it ends on the Season header; no era gates on the track.
verdict_why: Confirmed. The track draws 'ERA II · THE STILL HOUR' and 'ERA III' gates before tiers 11 and 21 (screens_meta.js:626, markup line 267, season_pass_full.txt). None of §18.3's eight weekly eras (Heavy Stars ... Quiet Week) appears anywhere in screens_meta.js or screens_main.js. §23.2's Season row requires 'era'. The server serves GET /v1/era (http.mjs:10). D69 records that the build has no era screen. That the design redefines an era as a season chapter is new.

title: The free season track gives a Sage the document does not have (the Chronicler)
evidence: Design: 'Free at tier 30: The Chronicler' (markup 262); the free reward table puts the Chronicler portrait at tier 50 (screens_meta.js:153). Doc §18.2: 'The free track gives pages, Essence and a stray'; §11.7 lists four Sages unlocked by Keeper level ('Sages are earned through play and never sold'); the Chronicler appears in v3.6 only in §23.5's character-sheet table, which refuses its Rewind power. §23.5 does not list the track reward.
rec: No Sage on the track; the premium track may carry a Sage robe for an existing §11.7 Sage.
verdict_why: The deviation is real but mis-stated. Markup line 262 says 'Free at tier 30: The Chronicler', and the free list ends with portrait 'The Chronicler' (screens_meta.js:153). §18.2: 'The free track gives pages, Essence and a stray'. The finding says the Chronicler appears only in §23.5, but v3.6 §11.7 (txt line 6217) names it: 'The Chronicler (Time) and the Lamplighter (Energy) follow after launch ... earned and never sold'.
corrected: The free track's final reward is the Chronicler (markup line 262; screens_meta.js:153). §11.7 lists it as an after-launch Sage whose powers are written when it ships. §18.2's free track gives only pages, Essence and a stray. So the design hands out an unshipped Sage at launch and puts a Sage on a track that has none. The premium perks also offer a 'Chronicler robe' for that same unshipped Sage (screens_meta.js:681).

title: League season-end rewards: Starglass and pages for every league, 'highest league reached'
evidence: Design League road: Paradox pages ×60 + Starglass 120 … Ember pages ×10 + insight ×5, Dust pages ×5 (screens_meta.js:688); 'At the end of the season you get the rewards for the highest league you reached.' (markup 287). Doc §18.5: 'Star, Nova and Paradox leagues with season-end cosmetics'; §9.1: Starglass earned from 'Purchases; small amounts from the free season track'; §18.1: 'rewards are given by league'. Server: final league, cosmetic to Star/Nova/Paradox only (server/src/seasons.mjs:46–53, 178–203).
rec: Show what the server grants. State in §18.1 whether the reward follows the final or the highest league, and what Dust, Ember and Tide receive (with G27).
verdict_why: Confirmed. The League road (screens_meta.js:688) gives pages plus Starglass 120/80/40/20 to Paradox, Nova, Star and Tide, pages plus insight to Ember, and pages to Dust. Markup line 287: 'the rewards for the highest league you reached'. §9.1 earns Starglass only from 'Purchases; small amounts from the free season track'. §18.5 gives Star, Nova and Paradox 'season-end cosmetics'. The server grants a cosmetic to those three by final league (seasons.mjs:46-53, 178-203). G27 already asks what Dust, Ember and Tide receive. New here: 'highest' against final league, and Starglass and pages as league rewards.

title: 'Earn renown: +30 Heist won, +20 Defence held, −10 Vault raided' contradicts §12.9
evidence: Design: screens_meta.js:693; markup 285; the battle log repeats 'Foiled … −18' and 'Held +14' (screens_meta.js:829). Doc §12.9: 'Renown for a clean heist = 20 × (1 + (defender's Renown − raider's Renown) ÷ 1,000), kept between 8 and 40, then multiplied by the outcome … The defender gains or loses the mirror amount. A foiled heist costs the raider a flat 8.' Server implements §12.9 (server/src/seasons.mjs:1–35).
rec: The League tab states §12.9 in words; the log shows the server's numbers.
verdict_why: Confirmed. screens_meta.js:693 has fixed '+30 Heist won, +20 Defence held, −10 Vault raided', and the battle log (screens_meta.js:829) shows 'FOILED −18' and 'HELD +14'. §12.9 gives 20×(1+(defender−raider)÷1,000), kept between 8 and 40, times the outcome, with the defender taking the mirror amount and a flat −8 for a foiled raider. The server implements §12.9 (seasons.mjs:1-35). C14 was about the document's own foiled case, so it does not cover this. §23.5's 'Demo numbers' row names other figures.

title: Star chests after the last tier add an earning loop the track does not have
evidence: Design: 'AFTER TIER 30 · STAR CHESTS · One every 500 ★ · up to 10 a season' (markup 268). Doc §18.2: 'Fifty tiers'; nothing after the last tier; contents of a chest are undefined.
rec: Do not build unless written into §18.2 with contents and cap.
verdict_why: Confirmed in season_pass_full.txt: 'AFTER TIER 30 · STAR CHESTS · One every 500 ★ · up to 10 a season'. §18.2 gives fifty tiers and nothing after them. Chest contents are undefined anywhere. §23.5's 'Season track 30 → 50 tiers' row covers the tier count, not chests. A chest is new earnings, which §23.5 says a design cannot add.

title: The Starpass is offered with no money price on the Season screen
evidence: Design: Starpass bar '600 ✦' and sheet 'Buy for 600 Starglass … Paid through the App Store · Ask to Buy applies' for every band (markup 272, 290; season_buy_sheet.png, same for 13–15); the Shop card says '≈ €5.99' while '100 ✦ is always €1' makes 600 ✦ €6.00. Doc §22.1: 'Every price is shown in real money before purchase'; §19.12 'Every cosmetic shows its real-money price'.
rec: Show the store's localized price on the bar and the sheet; band-aware payment words (see the Shop cap finding).
verdict_why: Confirmed. The Starpass bar shows '600 ✦' and the sheet says 'Buy for 600 Starglass' and 'Paid through the App Store · Ask to Buy applies', with no money figure (season_buy_sheet.txt). The Shop card says '600 Starglass ≈ €5.99' while the pack row says '100 ✦ is always €1'. §22.1: 'Every price is shown in real money before purchase'. Under the owner's F41 answer the pass is a store product at the store's price, so this mostly follows from F41.

title: F41 must be decided before the Shop is drawn: the design prices everything in Starglass, the owner's answer removed it
evidence: Design: Starglass pill '480 = €4.80 +', tiles '120 ≈€1.20', packs 100–5,000 ✦ at €1–€50, 'No bonus packs … Starglass never expires', buy sheets paying in ✦ (markup 297, 306–307, 324; shop_bottom.png). v3.6 unchanged in §9.1, §9.5 ('Cosmetics: Starglass only'), §18.2 ('bought with Starglass'), §22.1 ('Starglass, in packs from about €1 to €50') and §19.12 ('only as a gift and season-pass wrapper'). Build follows the owner's F41 answer, 'there is no currency' (server/src/shop.mjs:1–13; client/scripts/shop_screen.gd:1–6); register F41 is still open.
rec: Confirm the F41 answer and amend §9.1, §9.5, §18.2 and §22.1 (the design's ✦ lines become money lines), or reverse it and rebuild a currency on the server. Decide before Shop and Season are drawn.
verdict_why: The facts check out. The Shop is drawn in Starglass (shop_full.txt: '480 = €4.80', packs 100-5,000 ✦, 'Starglass never expires'). v3.6 §9.1, §9.5, §18.2, §22.1 and §19.12 still have Starglass. server/src/shop.mjs:1-13 and client/scripts/shop_screen.gd:1-6 follow the owner's 'no currency' answer. F41 is still open. This is F41 restated plus one new fact: Screens v3 depends on the currency. It belongs as a note on F41, not a new item. Downgraded from blocking: the build already runs on the owner's answer, and what remains is the document edit.

title: The Shop and the Starpass sheet ignore §20.2's purchase row: no cap shown, one family-approval text for every band
evidence: Design: Payments 'Through the App Store · ASK TO BUY · With Family Sharing, a parent approves each purchase. Limits are set in Screen Time.' for all (screens_meta.js:817); cap computed only for 13–15 (€25, screens_meta.js:718) and never drawn (capBar unused; cCap: false at screens_meta.js:788–790); no 16–17 band; no adult summary; adult and 13–15 captures identical (sssfp_shots vs sssfp_shots_minor shop_confirm_set). Doc §20.2: 13–15 'Family approval where set up; €25 a month cap', 16–17 '€50 a month cap', 18+ 'Monthly spending summary'; §23.2 Shop must show 'spending cap for minors'. Not in §23.5.
rec: Band-aware payments panel and buy sheet for three bands, cap shown before purchase in words; the server already holds both caps and the summary.
verdict_why: Confirmed. capL is 25 for '13–15' and Infinity otherwise (screens_meta.js:718). cCap is false on every confirm sheet (screens_meta.js:788-790). sh.capBar (screens_meta.js:817) is never used in the markup. The Payments panel shows 'ASK TO BUY · a parent approves each purchase' to everyone. The adult and 13-15 shop_confirm_set captures are byte-identical. §20.2 gives €25 with family approval for 13-15, €50 for 16-17 and a summary for adults. §23.2 Shop requires a 'spending cap for minors'. Settings (screens_meta.js:926) does draw a band-aware cap, so only the Shop and the Starpass sheet are wrong. D64 records that family approval is not built on the server, which is the server side only.
corrected: The Shop's Payments panel and every buy sheet, the Starpass sheet included, show the same Ask to Buy and family-approval text to every age band and never show a cap. Settings already draws one band by band (screens_meta.js:926). Per §20.2, the Shop needs the €25 cap with family approval for 13-15, the €50 cap for 16-17 and the monthly summary for adults.

title: No preview on the player's universe (Shop must-show)
evidence: Design: 'PREVIEW ON MY UNIVERSE' only calls G('home') with a toast 'Previewing Lantern Festival' (screens_meta.js:779); the item page shows a generic pedestal (shop_detail_realmskin.png). §23.2 Shop: 'previews on your universe'.
rec: Preview realm skins, skies and bridges on the player's own universe in the shared 3D world, unsaved; outfits on the player's own ruleborn.
verdict_why: Real but overstated. 'PREVIEW ON MY UNIVERSE' exists on the featured set, but its handler only shows a toast and opens Home (screens_meta.js:779). The outfit page has 'TRY IT ON', and the realm skin page has no preview control (shop_detail_*.txt). §23.2 Shop requires 'previews on your universe'. client/scripts/shop_screen.gd has no preview at all.
corrected: The design has the entry points ('PREVIEW ON MY UNIVERSE' on the featured set, 'TRY IT ON' on outfits) but never draws the preview itself. The button goes to an unchanged Home with a toast. Single realm skins, skies and bridges have no preview control. The build's shop has no preview either. The §23.2 must-show needs drawing and building.

title: The wishlist promises a 'back in the shop' notification
evidence: Design: 'On your wishlist. We tell you when it is back' (screens_meta.js:741). Doc §14.6: notifications 'only for things the player can act on (storage full, a character rested, an experiment finished, a heist against you)'; §19.12 refuses offers timed to weakness.
rec: A private wishlist without notifications, or none.
verdict_why: Confirmed. togWish says 'On your wishlist. We tell you when it is back' (screens_meta.js:741). The rule basis is weaker than claimed. §14.6 allows notifications for 'things the player can act on', and buying a returned item is arguably actionable. Even so, the doc lists no shop notification, and §23.5 says a design does not add what a player can hear. The wishlist itself is not in the document either. No register item (G34 covers notification timing only).
corrected: The wishlist promises a 'back in the shop' notification. No section lists one, and §23.5 does not let a design add it. Either write it into §14.6 or drop it; the same goes for the wishlist.

title: §22.4's monthly gift limit has no number; the design uses three and gives with no recipient or payment
evidence: Design: 'GIFT · 3 left this month'; tap says 'Gift sent to Ines · a parent approves first' for adults too, with no friend picker or payment (screens_meta.js:718, 819; shop_gift.png). Doc §22.4: 'with a monthly limit and parental approval rules for minors' (no number); D64 records the missing number.
rec: Adopt 3 a month into §22.4 (via §23.5's adopted table) or set another; the gift flow picks a friend and pays like a purchase, approval words for minors only.
verdict_why: Confirmed. gLeft defaults to 3, and the gift tap says 'Gift sent to Ines · a parent approves first' for every band, with no friend picker and no payment (screens_meta.js:718, 819; shop_gift.txt). §22.4 gives 'a monthly limit and parental approval rules for minors' with no number. D64 already records the missing number and the unbuilt approval rules. New here: the design proposes 3 a month.

title: Posting a clip to the Beacon: what is stored, who may watch, what a moment's rarity means, and whether 13–15 may post
evidence: Design: 'Post to the Beacon · Friends see it in their Beacon feed'; moments graded EPIC/RARE/LEGENDARY (screens_meta.js:1221–1229); same for 13–15. Doc §24 Clips: 'no video is stored on the server unless shared'; §17.6 feed 'Visible to friends in the game'. Owner's G35 answer: 13–15 heists appear in no feed (server/src/friends.mjs:79–100). No rule defines a moment's rarity. GET /v1/heists/:token/replay serves only raider and defender (http.mjs:11).
rec: Post the replay window, not a video; friends re-render it while the replay is kept; decide whether 13–15 may post; give rarity a rule or drop it.
verdict_why: Partly right. 'Post to the Beacon · Friends see it in their Beacon feed' and the EPIC/RARE/LEGENDARY moment grades are confirmed (screens_meta.js:1221-1229), and they are the same for 13-15. The storage point is wrong: the §24 Clips row ('no video is stored on the server unless shared') allows storing a clip once it is posted. The real gaps are two. A 13-15 can post to the feed, which G35's decided answer forbids (friends.mjs:84-100). And no rule defines a moment's rarity.
corrected: The design lets 13-15 players post clips to the Beacon feed, which G35's answer excludes them from (server/src/friends.mjs:84-100). It also grades moments EPIC/RARE/LEGENDARY with no rule behind the grade. Storing a posted clip is allowed by §24's 'unless shared'.

title: Friend status names the target while a raid happens ('Raiding Ines')
evidence: Design: FRL status 'Raiding Ines' shown on the friend row, the RAIDING pill and the sheet (screens_meta.js:1241; friends_list.png, friends_sheet_kofi.png). Doc §17.8: 'raids are anonymous while they happen'; the design's own feed footer: 'Raids show no names while they happen.'
rec: 'Raiding' without a target, or no live status at all (see presence finding).
verdict_why: Confirmed. FRL gives Kofi the status 'Raiding Ines' (screens_meta.js:1241), shown on the list and the sheet (friends_list.txt, friends_sheet_kofi.txt). §17.8 says 'raids are anonymous while they happen', and the design's own feed footer says 'Raids show no names while they happen.' If Ines is Kofi's friend she can see who is raiding her. Not in §23.5 or the register.

title: Presence, last seen and preset pings between friends are not in the document
evidence: Design: '3 online', ONLINE/OFFLINE sections, 'Seen 3 h ago', RAIDING/WORKSHOP/HOME pills, SEND A PING (Good heist!, Rematch?, Raid me!, Nice defence!) (screens_meta.js:1241–1285; markup 607–623), identical for 13–15. v3.6 defines no presence or friend messaging at launch (preset pings only for 1.1 co-op, §12.11); §20.2 profile private for 13–15 and by default for 16–17; §20.5 collect only what is needed; §14.6 notifications only when actionable. These change what a player can see and do, so §23.5 forbids adopting them from the design.
rec: Decide whether presence and pings ship at launch; if yes, write them into §17.6 with what 13–15 and 16–17 show to friends, a ping's daily cap, and whether a ping notifies.
verdict_why: Mostly right. '3 online', ONLINE/OFFLINE sections, 'Seen 3 h ago', the RAIDING/WORKSHOP/HOME pills and SEND A PING are all confirmed, and the 13-15 captures are identical (friends_list_full.txt matches). No section of v3.6 defines presence, last-seen or activity status, which is a privacy question for 13-15 (§20.2 profile private) and §20.5. Preset pings have a partial home: §20.2's Chat row gives 13-15 'Preset phrases and emotes only', so preset-phrase messaging exists in the document, just not between friends.
corrected: Presence, last-seen and live activity status between friends are not in the document, and the design shows them unchanged to 13-15 friends. Writing them in needs a decision on what each band reveals. The preset pings fit §20.2's preset-phrase chat but need a home in §17.6, saying whether a ping notifies and how many may be sent.

title: The Profile's outcome donut mislabels two outcomes and its won/lost split counts a Partial as lost
evidence: screens_meta.js:855 "dL: … ['CLEAN', 'PARTIAL', 'CAUGHT', 'FOILED'][ds]" against slices Clean, Loud, Partial, Foiled (stats_donut_loud.png shows '87 PARTIAL' for Loud); 128 won = Clean 41 + Loud 87 and 52 lost = Partial 38 + Foiled 14 (screens_meta.js:850, 852). Doc §12.9: four outcomes; Partial pays ×0.4 and Renown ×0.5; 'CAUGHT' is no outcome.
rec: Name each slice by its outcome; show the split by outcome, or define 'won' in §12.9.
verdict_why: Confirmed. The slices are Clean 41, Loud 87, Partial 38 and Foiled 14 (screens_meta.js:851), but dL labels them ['CLEAN','PARTIAL','CAUGHT','FOILED'] (screens_meta.js:855), so Loud reads '87 PARTIAL' (stats_donut_loud.txt). '128 won / 52 lost' (screens_meta.js:850) counts Clean+Loud as won and Partial+Foiled as lost. §12.9 has four outcomes and none is called 'Caught', and a Partial still pays ×0.4 and Renown ×0.5.

title: Badges and titles are Profile must-shows with no definition
evidence: Doc §23.2 Profile: 'collection and badges'; §18.5: mastery 'Milestones unlock titles'; §18.7 names only the creator badge. Design proposes nine badges with bronze/silver/gold thresholds (screens_meta.js:830: First heist, Ghost, Vault breaker, Iron wall, Law hunter, Resonant, Hoarder, Friendly, Paradox) and a title 'Quiet Thief' (markup 333).
rec: List the launch badges and titles, each paying nothing, in §23.5's adopted table or §18.5; give the server their counters.
verdict_why: Real with one qualification. §23.2 Profile requires 'collection and badges'. The only badge defined is §18.7's creator badge, plus §14.9's mastery title ('A title, and that school's laws get a visual style'). The design's nine graded badges (screens_meta.js:830) and 'Title · Quiet Thief' (markup line 333) have no definition. Titles do have a source in mastery (§14.9, §18.5), but 'Quiet Thief' is not a school-mastery title.
corrected: Badges are a §23.2 must-show with only §18.7's creator badge defined. Titles come from school mastery (§14.9, §18.5), yet the design shows a non-mastery title ('Quiet Thief'). The launch badges and any other titles need listing.

title: The Profile's records need per-heist facts nothing keeps, and its log promises 'the last 25 raids'
evidence: Design records and charts: escape time, alarms per heist, guards slept past, crew knocked out, most realms in one raid, entry edge ('Raiders come in over the west bridge'), favourite law, minutes played a day (screens_meta.js:844–880); 'Your last 25 raids are kept here.' (markup 362). Server verdict holds only grade, out, caught, crew, banked, capacity, pages, cracked, left (server/src/sim.mjs:103–107); laws crossed only in pseudonymous telemetry (service.mjs ~632); pages, forms and roster are on the device (D64). Doc §24.3: raw replays kept 30 to 90 days; §20.5 analytics pseudonymous.
rec: Write the needed per-heist facts at settle from the re-simulation (sim event log); keep log rows longer than replays and say when a replay is gone; derive the calendar from days with a validated heist or defence unless minutes are wanted, then decide their source.
verdict_why: Confirmed. The server verdict holds grade, out, caught, crew, banked, capacity, pages, cracked and left (server/src/sim.mjs:103-107). 'left' is unbanked loot, not time left (sim/src/heist.rs:162-166), so escape time, alarm count, guards slept past, entry edge and minutes played are not kept. The laws are recoverable from the lease's island bundle, and crew caught is kept. Markup line 362 says 'Your last 25 raids are kept here', while §24.3 keeps raw replays 30 to 90 days.

title: §17.8's 'a raid takes nothing' is false in §9.4's Open Vault league, which has no screen and no build
evidence: §17.8: 'Their island can still appear as a target … a raid takes nothing: there is no harm to be protected from'. §9.4: 'Players who want real stakes opt into the Open Vault league, where the rules below apply in full and rewards are 40% higher on both sides' (loot leaves the defender). The design's block sheet repeats §17.8 (screens_meta.js:1284). Neither Screens v3's League tab nor server/sim/client has the Open Vault league (grep finds none); the register has no item for it.
rec: Say in §17.8 what blocking does for Open Vault players (for example, a block removes each from the other's Open Vault targets); give the Open Vault opt-in a §23.2 home (the League tab) and a roadmap task, or move it after launch.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §17.8 rests blocking on 'a raid takes nothing: there is no harm to be protected from'. §9.4 has an opt-in Open Vault league 'where the rules below apply in full', with loot leaving the defender, and §27.5 (txt lines 9955, 13108) has soft launch reporting both leagues. The design's block sheet repeats 'because a raid takes nothing' (friends_block.txt). No Open Vault exists in Screens v3, server/, client/ or sim/, and no register or roadmap item mentions it.

title: The age-band preview changes the player's band, so a 13-15 player can switch off their own fixed protections
evidence: meta.js 946 bandOpts sets stg.band; meta.js 889 'band = S2.band ?? (props.ageBand === "13–15" ? 0 : 2)'; ptLock/qhOn read it (meta.js 897-898). Captured: as 13-15, Account → 18+ → header 'AGE 18+', play-time reminder and quiet hours set Off (scratchpad/analysis/sf_shots/minor_un_w_after18_offs.png). §23.5 lists only the highlight and the open look.
rec: Effective band only from AgeCheck/the server; comparison as a read-only sheet that changes no lock.
verdict_why: Confirmed. meta.js 946 bandOpts calls setK('band', i), and meta.js 889 derives band from S2.band, so ptLock and qhOn (meta.js 897-898) and the header pill all follow the preview. The design labels the control as a preview: markup 419 reads 'Set from your device's age check. Preview other bands here.' In practice it changes the effective band. The capture sf_shots/minor_un_w_after18_offs.png shows a 13-15 player at 'AGE 18+' with the play-time reminder Off. Quiet hours still reads On in that capture, but its Off segment is now live (minor=false). §20.2 fixes these protections for 13-15, and §24 (line 11664) says bands come from the platform. §23.5's 'Locked protections' and 'Account tab' rows cover how the rows look and which segment is highlighted. Neither covers the preview changing the band.
corrected: Settings → Account → Preview writes the band every lock reads. Previewing 18+ as a 13-15 player switches the play-time reminder Off at once (18+'s default) and unlocks quiet hours, which can then be switched Off. The capture shows the reminder Off and quiet hours still On but unlocked.

title: The age check is not neutral: 13 to 15 pre-selected and a way back from under 13
evidence: flBand: 1 default (meta.js 7, 963) pre-selects '13 to 15' (fl_01_age.png); under-13 stop has 'CHANGE AGE RANGE' (markup 452). §20.11: 'A neutral age gate, no accounts below 13 … the gate is not decorative'. Client already neutral (client/scripts/age_screen.gd:3-5; client/data/age_check.gd:86-94). §23.5 says the first launch already follows the document.
rec: No pre-selection, no way back from under 13; the platform's prompt where it exists, otherwise the game's own neutral question (not drawn as an OS sheet).
verdict_why: Confirmed. flBand defaults to 1 (meta.js 7, 963), and fl_01_age.png shows '13 to 15' already selected. The under-13 stop has a 'CHANGE AGE RANGE' button (markup 452) wired to fl.toAge, which goes back to the question. §20.11 asks for 'A neutral age gate, no accounts below 13 … the gate is not decorative'. §23.5 (line 11418) claims the first launch already follows the document. The client's fallback suggests no answer and never asks again after under 13 (client/scripts/age_screen.gd:3-5). The second cited client location is wrong: the rule sits at client/data/age_check.gd:43-50, and that file has only 77 lines, so 86-94 does not exist. Where the platform draws its own prompt the game controls neither the sheet nor its pre-selection, but the way back from under 13 is the game's own screen.
corrected: The design's age step pre-selects '13 to 15' and lets an under-13 answer go back and change the range. Neither is neutral (§20.11). The client already does this right: client/scripts/age_screen.gd:3-5 and client/data/age_check.gd:43-50.
existing: none (D70 covered only the age check's absence, since built)

title: The purchases protection omits §20.2's caps and the adult summary in Settings and First launch
evidence: PROT meta.js 906 and FPROT meta.js 954: 13-15 'Ask to Buy · a parent approves', 16-17/18+ 'Through the App Store'; markup 420 'A parent … gets a monthly summary'. §20.2: '€25 a month cap', '€50 a month cap', 18+ 'Monthly spending summary'. v3.6 §23.2 Settings: 'any protection the age band fixes is shown locked'. Same root as SS11 (Shop) in screens-season-shop-share-friends-stats.md.
rec: Show the band's cap and this month's spending (GET /v1/shop/summary) in both places; drop the parent monthly summary unless built.
verdict_why: Confirmed. PROT (meta.js 906) and FPROT (meta.js 954) give 13-15 Ask to Buy and give 16-17 and 18+ 'Through the App Store'. §20.2 gives 13-15 'Family approval where set up; €25 a month cap', 16-17 '€50 a month cap' and 18+ 'Monthly spending summary'. The Settings code does compute a 13-15 cap (zcapL 25, capT, meta.js 901 and 926), but the markup never renders it: no stg.capT in screens_meta.markup.html. Markup 420 promises that a parent 'gets a monthly summary', which §20.2 does not say. The v3.6 §23.2 Settings row requires fixed protections to be shown. Not in §23.5. The register's D64 covers only the server's cap.
corrected: Settings and First launch both show Purchases without §20.2's caps (€25 and €50) or the adult monthly summary. The €25 cap is computed in meta.js 901/926 but never drawn. The 13-15 Family approval card adds a parent monthly summary that §20.2 does not give.

title: First launch tells a 13-15 player 'A parent can change these in Settings'
evidence: meta.js 978 setSub: 13-15 'A parent can change these in Settings.'; 16-17 'You can loosen chat yourself; the rest stays on.' §20.9: '13 to 15 cannot'; §20.2 16-17 profile 'Private by default', reminder 'Every 90 minutes by default'.
rec: Per-band lines that match §20.2 (13-15: these stay on until 16).
verdict_why: Confirmed at meta.js 978. §20.2 fixes 13-15's chat, night and play reminder, and §20.9 says '13 to 15 cannot' move to free chat. Neither the document nor the design has a parent control that loosens these. The 16-17 line 'the rest stays on' is also wrong: §20.2 gives 16-17 a profile that is 'Private by default' and a reminder 'Every 90 minutes by default', so both can change.

title: The first session ends at Keeper 3 with 'Level 4 opens your first outer realm'
evidence: meta.js 998 rvLvT 'KEEPER LEVEL 2'/'KEEPER LEVEL 3'; markup 462 'Level 4 opens your first outer realm'. §5.2 'Outer realms open at Keeper levels 3, 6, 10…'; §14.2 level 3 'Outer realm 1 and its Nursery'; §16 10:00 'the next realm two levels away'. Not in §23.5's first-session row.
rec: Show the server's level; 'Keeper 3 opens your first outer realm'.
verdict_why: Confirmed. meta.js 998 sets rvLvT to 'KEEPER LEVEL 2' and then 'KEEPER LEVEL 3', and markup 462 reads 'Keeper level 3 … Level 4 opens your first outer realm'. §5.2 (line 655) says 'Outer realms open at Keeper levels 3, 6, 10…'. §14.2's level-3 row is 'Outer realm 1 and its Nursery'. §16's 10:00 beat says 'the next realm two levels away', so the session ends at Keeper 1. §23.5's First session row does not cover Keeper levels.

title: Five of §16's moments are missing from the first-launch design
evidence: MOM meta.js 955-962, RV meta.js 964: no note Flow at 0:30 ('The page shows the law's one note, Flow'); no ability shown at 1:15; Star Well only, no Garden or Hearth at 5:00; the 7:00 ruin chosen but never run; no insight pages or tired crew at 10:00. §23.2 must-show: 'the moments in section 16'.
rec: Run each beat on its real screen (heist, weaving, roster, Lab, Observatory) and show the note.
verdict_why: Confirmed against MOM/RV (meta.js 955-964) and the done markup. Nothing shows the note Flow, which §16 0:30 and §8.6 line 4317 require. Abilities are only described in a sentence ('Featherkin scouts, Emberling breaks, Tidewalker swims'), not shown. 5:00 sends the strays to the Star Well only, with no Garden. 7:00 chooses a ruin and goes straight to the Lab without running it. 10:00 has no insight pages and no tired crew. §23.2 must show 'the moments in section 16', and §23.5 lists only the Essence, stability and built-Heart differences. One nuance: the Hearth does appear at 1:15 ('sleeping by the Hearth'). The 5:00 beat simply does not show the strays going to a free Hearth.
corrected: Missing from the design's beats: the note Flow (0:30), each ruleborn showing its ability (1:15), the Garden and the strays' free Hearth (5:00), running the chosen ruin (7:00), and the insight pages and tired crew (10:00).

title: SKIP ends the first session with its whole haul
evidence: skip (meta.js 1014) → done; haul constant 3 laws / 5 ruleborn / 1 resonance (meta.js 1018). §25.2: 'Every first session ends with the player having robbed a vault and woven a law into their own island'. Granting rewards without play changes what a player earns (§23.5 mechanic rule).
rec: No skip in the first session, or skip only for an account that completed it elsewhere.
verdict_why: Confirmed. skip (meta.js 1014) jumps to the done screen, which shows a constant haul (meta.js 1018) and 'Session 1 DONE'. Part of the stated reason does not hold: 3 laws and 5 ruleborn are §14.2's level-1 unlocks, so getting them without play is not a new earning. What a skip does break is §25.2's 'Every first session ends with the player having robbed a vault and woven a law'. It also hands over the first resonance and two Keeper levels without play.
corrected: The first session's SKIP ends the session without a robbed vault or a woven law, which breaks §25.2's 'one meaningful action' rule, and the done screen still credits the resonance and the Keeper levels. The 3 laws and 5 ruleborn match §14.2's level-1 unlocks.

title: v3.6 gives three times for the first heist and two answers on whether minute one is guided
evidence: §15.2 'Moving the crew … | Minute 1 | A guided first heist in a ruin'; §16 '2:00 | First heist'; §25.2 'Median time to the first heist | Under 45 seconds' and 'The first minute is unguided play'. §23.5's adopted order adds title, age check, protections and the Keeper name before §16's 0:00.
rec: One time and one rule: move the heist into minute one, or restate §25.2's median from the end of the age check with a reachable figure.
verdict_why: All quoted texts confirmed. §15.2 has 'Moving the crew, abilities, the Vault, calling the skiff | Minute 1 | A guided first heist in a ruin'. §16 has '2:00 | First heist'. §25.2 has 'Median time to the first heist | Under 45 seconds' and 'The first minute is unguided play'. §23.5's adopted order puts the title, age check, protections and Keeper name before §16's 0:00. This is a contradiction inside v3.6 and needs the owner's decision.

title: 'No account creation, no permission prompts before the first heist' against the platform age check and the adopted Keeper name
evidence: §25.2 'No account creation, no permission prompts, no settings and no logos that can't be skipped before the first heist'; §20.1 asks the platform at first launch (Declared Age Range is a system prompt); §23.5 adopts 'the Keeper's name and face' before the beats.
rec: State the age check is the one prompt before play; the Keeper name is kept on the phone and the account made after the first heist.
