verdict_why: §25.2's Playing within 30 seconds row says 'No account creation, no permission prompts, no settings and no logos that can't be skipped before the first heist'. §20.1 and §24 (line 11664) ask the platform for the band at first launch, and the design itself draws that as a system 'Share your age range?' sheet. §23.5 adopts the protections summary and the Keeper name before the beats. The tension is real but depends on reading: a name is not necessarily account creation, and Google's age signals show no prompt. It needs one sentence of wording, not a design change.

title: The first session's weaves have no stated time against §5.6's ten minutes
evidence: §5.6 '10 minutes at tier I … While a slot is being woven it is empty'; §16 weaves Half gravity at 0:30 and Bloom at 6:30 and shows the stability bar at once inside ten minutes; the design weaves instantly.
rec: Say in §16 that tutorial weaves are instant (or only the first).
verdict_why: §5.6 (line 965) says 'Laws are woven … 10 minutes at tier I … While a slot is being woven it is empty', at 40 Aether per point. §16 weaves Half gravity at 0:30, with stones lifting at once, and Bloom at 6:30, with the stability bar shown at once, all inside ten minutes. §16 never says tutorial weaves are exempt. The design weaves instantly.

title: Settings offers 'Season rewards' notifications and lacks 'an experiment finished'
evidence: notes meta.js 937: You were raided, Buildings ready, Crew rested, Weaving done, Season rewards. §14.6 '(storage full, a character rested, an experiment finished, a heist against you)'; §18.8 'no notification when a season is ending'; server deliberately has none (server/src/notifications.mjs:10-12).
rec: Storage full, Crew rested, Experiment finished, Weaving done (§5.6 timed), You were raided; no Season rewards.
verdict_why: Confirmed. notes (meta.js 937) lists You were raided, Buildings ready, Crew rested, Weaving done and Season rewards. §14.6 allows notifications 'only for things the player can act on (storage full, a character rested, an experiment finished, a heist against you)'. §18.8 forbids a notification when a season is ending, and the server deliberately sends nothing else (server/src/notifications.mjs:10-12). The design is missing 'an experiment finished' and adds 'Season rewards'. One inconsistency in the finding: its recommendation keeps 'Weaving done', which is not in §14.6's list either.
corrected: The design's notification list is not §14.6's. It lacks 'an experiment finished', words 'storage full' as 'Buildings ready', and adds 'Season rewards' and 'Weaving done', neither of which §14.6 lists. Season rewards also sits against §18.8's no-pressure rule. Under §23.5's mechanic rule, neither added kind is built until it is written into the document.

title: The daily reminder is on at 18:30 by default
evidence: rtOpts default index 1 (meta.js 923), visible in st_w_mid.png. §14.6 'Players choose a daily reminder time, or none'; §14.10 'No win-back pressure'; server reminder_at null by default (server/src/db.mjs:55).
rec: Off until the player picks a time.
verdict_why: Confirmed. rtOpts is sgO('rt', ['12:00','18:30','20:00','Off'], 1) at meta.js 923, and stg holds no rt, so 18:30 is selected by default. §14.6 says 'Players choose a daily reminder time, or none'. The server stores none until the player chooses one (server/src/db.mjs:55, reminder_at with no default). Low risk, because the build follows the document.

title: §14.6 says nothing is sent at night; §20.2 lets adults open the night
evidence: §14.6 'nothing is sent at night (see 20.2)'; §20.2 18+ 'Off 22:00 to 08:00 by default'. Server and design follow §20.2 (notifications.mjs header lines 9-11; design adult Quiet hours On/Off).
rec: §14.6: 'nothing is sent at night unless an adult chooses otherwise (20.2)'.
verdict_why: §14.6 says 'nothing is sent at night (see 20.2)'. §20.2's 18+ row says 'Off 22:00 to 08:00 by default', which lets an adult open the night. The cross-reference softens the conflict, but read literally the two sentences disagree. The server already follows §20.2 (notifications.mjs:9-11). This is a one-line wording fix in §14.6.

title: Play-time reminder: whether 16-17 may turn it off and what 'every 60 minutes' counts
evidence: §20.2 16-17 'Every 90 minutes by default'. Design lets 16-17 pick Off (PT_O meta.js 897), counts the day's total ('38 MIN TODAY' → 'Pause card in 22 min', meta.js 911-915) and draws the interval as a line across daily bars (limLine), reading as a daily limit the document does not have.
rec: Say whether Off is allowed at 16-17 and whether the interval is continuous play or the day's total; draw it as an interval.
verdict_why: Confirmed. PT_O includes Off and ptLock is band===0 only (meta.js 897), so 16-17 can pick Off. Against today's 38 minutes the design shows 'Pause card in 22 min' (meta.js 911-919), and limLine draws the interval across the daily bars. §20.2 gives 16-17 'Every 90 minutes by default' and 18+ 'Optional'. That contrast suggests 16-17 may not turn the reminder off, but the document never says so, nor what the interval counts. A §20.2 protection needs the owner's decision.

title: Settings lacks hold times, movable controls, help and support, and profile visibility
evidence: Access tab rows (meta.js 944-945) have no hold time or control layout; §20.8 'controls can be mirrored … and moved; hold times adjustable' and §12.7 'Hold to choose where the skiff comes'. No Help/Support anywhere in the screens (grep of both markups); §20.10 'an in-game help section and a ticket form', §20.11 'published contact details' (server serves /support). No profile visibility control though §20.2 gives 16-17 'Private by default' and 18+ 'Player's choice'.
rec: Add Hold time, Move controls, Help and support, Licences and a band-aware Profile visibility row.
verdict_why: Confirmed. The Access rows (meta.js 944-945) have no hold time and no control layout, against §20.8 Moving: 'controls can be mirrored … and moved; hold times adjustable', and §12.7 has a hold on Get out. No help, support or contact appears anywhere in either markup or logic file. §20.10 requires 'an in-game help section and a ticket form', and §20.11 requires 'published contact details'. No screen offers a profile-visibility control, although §20.2 gives 16-17 'Private by default' and 18+ 'Player's choice'. Not in §23.5.

title: The deletion line drops the choice to withdraw islands
evidence: meta.js 951 'You will be asked twice. Your islands stay as unnamed ruins.' §20.12 'or be withdrawn entirely at the player's request'; server takes withdrawIslands (server/src/http.mjs:567-572, F43).
rec: Offer 'Withdraw my islands too' in the second confirmation.
verdict_why: Confirmed at meta.js 951: 'You will be asked twice. Your islands stay as unnamed ruins.' §20.12 says the island 'may remain as an unnamed derelict … or be withdrawn entirely at the player's request'. The server already takes withdrawIslands (server/src/http.mjs:567-572, commented 'F43: the deletion screen's withdraw my islands too').

title: How an age band changes is unwritten, and the server accepts any band from the device
evidence: Design: 'You can change it later with a parent' (markup 439). §20.1/§24 take the band from the platform; nothing on birthdays, platform updates or wrong answers. PUT /v1/age stores any band at any time (server/src/http.mjs:528-537; server/src/workshop.mjs:89-93).
rec: Bands change only by a new platform signal, or only toward more protection from the device.
verdict_why: Confirmed. PUT /v1/age (server/src/http.mjs:528-537) passes any band other than under-13 to setAgeBand, and server/src/workshop.mjs:89-93 stores it at any time. Nothing in the server checks direction or source. The design says 'You can change it later with a parent' (markup 439). §20.1 and §24 take the band from the platform and say nothing about changes. As built, a modified client can loosen a minor's protections. D62 notes only that the band is 'declared, not verified'.

title: Whether raiders see a 13-15 player's Keeper name
evidence: §12.4 free information: 'name, Keeper level, number of realms, Renown…'; §20.2 13-15 profile 'Private'. Design shows 'HOW RAIDERS SEE YOU: Wren' for every band (markup 448).
rec: Say whether the Keeper name is part of the private profile, and whether 13-15 names come from word lists.
verdict_why: Confirmed. Markup 448 shows 'HOW RAIDERS SEE YOU {{ fl.name }} Keeper level 1 · 1 realm · Unranked' for every band. §12.4's free information starts with 'name'. §20.2 makes a 13-15 profile 'Private', and the document never says whether the Keeper name is part of that profile. This touches minors' privacy and needs the owner's decision.

title: Consent by country and the terms gate have no place in the first launch
evidence: §20.5 'consent follows the player's country'; §20.11 Google 'a terms-of-use gate'. The design's first launch has neither; the server asks for terms only before Workshop actions (server/src/safety.mjs header).
rec: Say whether a player below their country's consent age needs a parent's consent and where the terms are accepted.
verdict_why: §20.5 says 'consent follows the player's country', and §20.11 lists Google's 'a terms-of-use gate'. Neither appears in the design's first launch: title → age → setup → name → play. The document does not say where they go or what a below-consent-age 13-15 player needs. The register has no consent item; its mentions of consent at lines 727, 8168 and 9384 concern pre-release testing.

title: Access tab: Stillness text and two school shapes differ from the document
evidence: markup 406 'invisible to guards.' vs §7.7 'invisible to guards and wards.'; SCH meta.js 902 Matter hexagon, Spirit oval vs §5.2 cube and eye. §23.5 lists only the Life gem for this panel.
rec: Use §7.7's text from content and §5.2's shapes.
verdict_why: Markup 406 reads 'invisible to guards.', while §7.7 (lines 1942 and 2800) and content/laws.json:379 read 'invisible to guards and wards.'. That difference is new. SCH (meta.js 902) draws Spirit as a plain ellipse, where §5.2 gives an eye. That is also new and minor. Matter is drawn as a flat hexagon outline, which is the silhouette of a cube without its inner edges. §23.5 already lists this under 'Matter's shape | Called a hexagon | A cube; drawn in three-quarter view it keeps its inner edges', in the character-sheet table.
corrected: The Access tab quotes Stillness without 'and wards' (§7.7) and draws Spirit as a plain oval rather than an eye (§5.2). Its flat-hexagon Matter is the same difference §23.5's 'Matter's shape' row records, so only the text and the Spirit shape are new.

title: First-session labels teach the wrong thing: Swimmer as a role, stars, 'Keep it green', 'Name it'
evidence: RV meta.js 964 'Scout · Breaker · Swimmer' (Swimmer is a §11.3 trait; Tidewalker is a Carrier); three stars on HEIST WON (markup 457) vs §12.9 outcomes; MOM meta.js 960 'Keep it green' vs §5.5 bands paying more up to Brimming; 'Name it' though the experiment names the resonance (§16).
rec: Roles, the outcome name, band names, 'See what it made'.
verdict_why: Confirmed. RV[2] reads 'Scout · Breaker · Swimmer' (meta.js 964), but §11.2 makes a Tidewalker a Carrier (line 6034) and §11.3 makes Swimmer a trait (line 6142). The first heist's reveal shows ★ stars (markup 457, rvStars), where §12.9 has outcomes: Clean, Loud, Partial, Foiled. MOM[5] says 'Keep it green' (meta.js 960), against §5.5's bands, which pay more up to Brimming. The 10:00 button reads 'Name it', but in §16 the experiment names Mangrove banks. §23.5's Roster row covers the Tidewalker's role on another screen, not this label.

title: Weaving renders neither the seven-band stability bar nor the harmonies and clashes a law would cause, though its code computes both
evidence: §23.2 (line 11225): 'stability bar with its seven bands, and the harmonies and clashes a law would cause before it's woven'. §15.3: 'Weaving preview | Shows harmonies, clashes and the stability band before committing | Always on'. §16 at 6:30 (line 8864): 'sees the stability bar for the first time'. §8.6: dissonance 'While weaving, with a warning'. screens_main.js:382 (sel.combos) and :384-386 (bands, mNow, mProj, seg, cons) are never bound in screens_main.markup.html:577-623. The screen shows '+3% = 85% → HUMMING' and a ♪ or ✕ glyph only. §23.5 (line 11418) says Weaving 'already follow[s] this document' and lists only 'No recommended laws'.
rec: Add a row to §23.5's table: Weaving shows neither the seven-band bar nor harmony and clash lines; the build follows §23.2, §15.3 and §8.6. The build renders the bar and the combination lines the design's own code computes.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §23.2 (line 11225) asks Weaving for a 'stability bar with its seven bands, and the harmonies and clashes a law would cause'. §15.3 (line 8780) requires a 'Weaving preview' that is always on, and §8.6 (line 4299) says dissonances show 'While weaving, with a warning'. screens_main.js computes the band bar (bands/mNow/mProj/seg at :384-387), the consequence text (cons/consTag at :388) and the named combo lines (sel.combos at :382). None of these is bound anywhere in screens_main.markup.html:578-623. The screenshot Gameplay_05_Weaving.png shows only '+3% = 85% → HUMMING' and a ♪ or ✕ badge on the deck cards, with no partner and no effect. §23.5 (line 11418) says Weaving 'already follow[s] this document' and lists only 'No recommended laws'. No register item covers this.

title: The Law card's WEAK AGAINST invents law-versus-law counters the document never states
evidence: screens_main.js:197 (CT): Static weak against 'Slow rivers: Water grounds the charge' and 'Glass: Glass walls carry no current'; Stillness against 'Haste: Hard to stop in time'; Glowing dark against 'Day and night: Light phases break the dark'. §7.7 gives one weakness per law (content/laws.json: Stillness 'Any Glow law breaks the hiding.'; Static 'Crews that bunch up get stunned together.'). No section states these law-on-law interactions and sim/ does not play them. §23.5 line 11391: 'A design never adds a mechanic.'
rec: Add to §23.5. The card's back shows §7.7's weakness, plus raider and defender use; no counters are built unless the document writes them.
verdict_why: Confirmed. screens_main.js:197 (CT) puts law-versus-law counters with invented reasons under 'WEAK AGAINST' on the card's back (markup:886). Examples: Static against Slow rivers ('Water grounds the charge') and Glass; Stillness against Haste; Glowing dark against Day and night. §7.7 gives exactly one weakness per law, and content/laws.json gives Static's as 'Crews that bunch up get stunned together.' and Stillness's as 'Any Glow law breaks the hiding.' No section states the design's interactions, so the card shows players rules that do not exist, against §23.5 ('A design never adds a mechanic'; the document wins on text). Only Stillness/Whispers loosely matches §7.7, because Whispers carries Glow, and even there the stated reason differs. Neither §23.5 nor the register lists it.

title: Law card face lacks the one-line rule, notes as symbols and pages
evidence: §21.7 (line 10980): 'Law card: the school shape and colour at the top, the law's name, a looping four-second preview of its movement signature, a one-line rule, notes as symbols, rank and tier pips.' §23.2 lists 'pages'. The design's front (screens_main.markup.html:874-877) has name, glyph, rank, tier pips and 'Restoring · 31%'; the rule and the notes (as words) are on the back only (markup:878-883). §23.5's Law card row covers only the school shape and the preview.
rec: Extend §23.5's Law card row. The build puts the rule, note symbols and 'N of M pages' (or the next tier's price) on the face.
verdict_why: Partly confirmed. On the front (markup:874-877, screenshot 03) there is the stability cost, name, tier pips, a pause glyph, rank, school, 'Mastered · Tier III' or 'Restoring · N%', and 'Woven in'. The one-line rule and the notes appear only on the back, and the notes are words ('COMMON · TIME · HUSH'), not the symbols §21.7 (line 10980) asks for. §21.7 never says the card has a single face, so the rule being on the back is only a weak deviation. Pages appear only as a percentage while restoring. §23.5's Law card row covers only the pause sign and the missing preview.
corrected: The Law card shows its notes as words on the back, not as symbols (§21.7), and puts the one-line rule only behind a flip. §21.7 does not name a face, so moving the rule is a recommendation, not a rule breach. Pages show only as 'Restoring · N%'.

title: Mastery is a per-law tier III in the design and an undefined per-school track in the document
evidence: Design: screens_main.js:196 (mastered = tier III), the 'Mastered · Tier III' star, and the Codex's '3 mastered' (screens_meta.js:391,406). §18.5: 'Mastery tracks | One per school, filled by crossing and weaving its laws. Milestones unlock titles and new visual styles'. §14.9: 'Master a school | Weave and cross every law of one school, at tier III, and win with each'. §23.2's Codex row asks for 'mastery'. No section gives what fills a track, by how much, or its milestones.
rec: Define the mastery track in §18.5: the events counted, the counts, the milestones and rewards. Tell the design to call tier III 'Tier III', not 'mastered'.
verdict_why: Confirmed. The design treats tier III as 'mastered' per law: screens_main.js lawX gives mast=cur===3 and tierTxt 'Mastered · Tier III', and screens_meta.js:391 has mastN and '… mastered' with ★ tiles. §18.5 (line 9039) makes mastery one track per school, 'filled by crossing and weaving its laws', with milestones but no counts, amounts or rewards. §14.9 (line 8504) defines the 'Master a school' goal, not the track. §23.2's Codex row (line 11257) requires 'mastery'. Neither the register nor §23.5 covers it.

title: §7.6 opens the Codex with '12 findable from the start' but never names the twelve
evidence: §7.6 (line 2215): 'at launch it holds the launch 24 (7), 12 findable from the start and all 24 from Keeper level 6 ... Matchmaking only shows universes running laws from open chapters.' tools/economy_model/model.py:617: 'Which laws each chapter holds is not stated by rank, so the cheapest remaining law is always taken to be open'. The Codex, matchmaking and ruins all need the list.
rec: List chapter 1's twelve, which must include the three starting laws (for example two per school), and give the same for later chapters as seasons add laws.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §7.6 (line 2215) and §14.2 (line 7760: 'Codex chapter 1 (12 laws)') never name the twelve. content/laws.json has no chapter field. tools/economy_model/model.py:617 says so in plain words and assumes the cheapest laws. The server has no chapter logic, although §7.6 says matchmaking filters by open chapters. Register items D6, Q5, C9 and C35 mention chapters but not which laws they hold.

title: Codex adds location hints and a 'Next lead' for unknown laws, some naming things that do not exist
evidence: screens_meta.js:396 (HINT): 'Win a storm heist', 'Spirit realms, level 8+' (realm levels stop at five, §9.6 line 4654), 'Energy realms at night', 'Seen in Mira's Hive', 'Rumoured near Verdant'; screens_meta.js:399-400: a NEXT LEAD card with SCOUT. §19.6: 'Unknown laws shown as "?"'. §7.6: a law joins the Codex on first meeting. This changes what a player can see, which §23.5 forbids a design to add.
rec: Add to §23.5. The build shows '?' tiles with no location hint until the document writes a lead rule, for example one reusing §12.15's offer reasons.
verdict_why: Confirmed. screens_meta.js:396 HINT gives unknown laws location leads: 'Seen in Mira's Hive', 'Spirit realms, level 8+' (§9.6 line 4654 says realm levels stop at five), 'Win a storm heist', 'Rumoured near Verdant'. :399 adds a NEXT LEAD spotlight, and the page text shows 'NEXT LEAD … Seen in Mira's Hive'. §19.6 (lines 9282, 9464) and §23.2 ask only for '?' tiles. Pointing players to where a law is changes what they can see, which §23.5 forbids a design to add. §23.5's Codex row covers only chapters versus schools.

title: 'Meeting' a law is undefined, yet it sets Codex entry, a page, and the complexity budget
evidence: §7.6 (line 2205): 'The first time a player meets a law it joins the Codex with 1 page.' §14.4: 'Meeting a law for the first time | 1'. §7.8: 'Laws on the route the player has never met'. §12.4: a paid scout shows each realm's laws. The design treats a scouted law as still unknown ('Seen in Mira's Hive'). Not stated: whether meeting means crossing its realm in a heist, being on the route, being scouted, meeting it in a ruin, or the Archivist handing it over.
rec: Define meeting in §7.6 (for example: a heist or ruin route enters a realm running it), and say whether scouting reveals the name without the page.
verdict_why: Confirmed. 'Meets a law' (§7.6 lines 2205, 2225), 'Meeting a law for the first time' (§14.4 line 8257) and 'Laws on the route the player has never met' (§7.8 line 3731) are never defined. The candidates are crossing its realm, being on the route, a scout report, a ruin, or the Archivist. The design treats a law seen through a scout as still unknown ('Seen in Mira's Hive'). The server does not implement Codex entry yet. No register item covers it.

title: What an owner sees of an undiscovered resonance or chord active in their own realm
evidence: §8.4 (line 3990): 'hidden until discovered in the Lab, or hinted at after crossing them'. §8.5 (line 4219): 'The Lab names chords'. §8.6: shown 'Once discovered'. §5.5 (line 845) applies ×0.8 per resonance, ×0.9 in a chord and the 192-point draw unconditionally, so Weaving's strain and the Harmony view's costs move by amounts the player cannot explain. The design names and celebrates them on first view (screens_meta.js:1080,1120,1128). The client already names them on the owner's island (client/scripts/builder_screen.gd:206-208).
rec: State one of two readings in §8.6. Either weaving all a resonance's or chord's laws discovers it (a new discovery path, written down), or it applies and shows as an unnamed 'something sounds here' until the Lab names it.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §8.4 (line 3990) hides resonances 'until discovered in the Lab, or hinted at after crossing'. §8.5 says the Lab names chords 'the player has woven or crossed', so an unnamed chord can be woven. §5.5 (line 845) applies ×0.8, ×0.9 and the draw whether or not the player knows. The design's Harmony view names them and shows a 'RESONANCE FOUND' or 'CHORD FORMED' celebration when the realm is first viewed (screens_meta.js:1080-1081, cel at ~1128), which is in effect a new way to discover them. client/scripts/builder_screen.gd:206-218 already names resonances and chords on the owner's island. Nothing in the document says what an owner sees before discovery. The register has nothing on it.

title: A crown law's cost when it harmonises or clashes in several realms
evidence: §8.2: 'Crown laws count in every realm, so a crown law can harmonise with every realm's laws. A harmony lowers the stability cost of both laws by 15%.' §5.5 prices one law once. §8.5's worked example (line 4227) has a crown law in one realm only. The design shows a different delta for Kinship in each realm (+25% Emberreach, ±0% Skyfield, −10% Tidehold; screens_meta.js:1076-1086).
rec: State in §5.5 whether a crown law's discounts and penalties compound across every realm, apply once, or are counted per realm in strain.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §8.2 (line 3926 area) says crown laws 'count in every realm, so a crown law can harmonise with every realm's laws'. §5.5's formula prices each law once, and its 'in a realm of its school' and 'for each harmony' have no reading for a law present in every realm. §8.5's worked example prices the crown law (Bloom) only at the Heart. The design gives Kinship a different cost change in each realm (screens_meta.js:1066 RL includes kinship in every realm; evalSet runs per realm). D61 is related (the simulation plays no crown laws) but does not cover cost.

title: How harmonies are counted: per shared note or per pair
evidence: §8.2: 'When two laws in the same realm share a note, they harmonise ... lowers the stability cost of both laws by 15%.' Open cases: three laws on one note (one harmony or three pairs); two laws sharing two notes (Haste and Frictionless share Flow and Spark). §8.5's example only fixes Thorns at ×0.85² with two different partners and notes. The design counts per pair per note in Weaving (screens_main.js:355) and once per note in Harmony (screens_meta.js:1077).
rec: Add one sentence to §8.2, mirrored in §5.5's formula.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §8.2 and §5.5 ('× 0.85 for each harmony') do not settle whether three laws on one note make one harmony or three pairs, or whether two laws sharing two notes make one harmony or two. §8.5's example (Thorns with two partners on two different notes) fits either reading. The design's two screens disagree. Weaving (screens_main.js:355-356, wCombos) counts each woven partner per shared note. Harmony view (screens_meta.js evalSet) applies ×0.85 once per note to every law carrying it. G25 records the simulation reading a harmony's effect 'once a note'; that is the effect side only, not cost.

title: The first session weaves laws instantly that §5.6 says take 10 minutes
evidence: §16 (line 8848) at 0:30: 'The player places it in their Heart. Stones lift'. Line 8864 at 6:30: Bloom woven and the player 'sees the stability bar'. The session ends at 10:00. §5.6 (line 965): 'Laws are woven into slots ... 10 minutes at tier I'; 'While a slot is being woven it is empty.' No exemption is written.
rec: State in §5.6 or §16 that first-session weaves (or each starting law's first weave) are instant.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §16 at 0:30 (line 8848): 'The player places it in their Heart. Stones lift'. At 6:30 (line 8864) Bloom is woven and the stability bar seen, and the session ends at 10:00. §5.6 (line 965): '10 minutes at tier I' and 'While a slot is being woven it is empty.' No exemption is written anywhere. §23.5's First session row covers other differences, not weave time. F56 (starting universe) does not cover it.

title: Upkeep is priced against 'the realm's stability budget', but stability exists only per universe
evidence: §5.6 (line 969): '25% when the realm's stability budget is fully spent ... a realm running laws worth half its stability pays 12.5%'. §9.5 and §29.1 repeat it. §5.5: 'Stability is how much law a universe can hold', with capacity and strain defined per universe only.
rec: Define a realm's share (for example its woven laws' cost ÷ capacity, with crown laws charged to the Heart or split), or price upkeep on the universe's total Aether production.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §5.6 (line 969) prices upkeep against 'the realm's stability budget' ('a realm running laws worth half its stability pays 12.5%'). §29.1 (line 13714) repeats it. §5.5 defines capacity and strain only per universe. One possible reading is each realm's own Anchor Stone (one per realm, +stability), with the Spire for the Heart, but it is never stated, and crown laws have no realm to charge. The server needs a definition to charge upkeep. F17 covers upkeep's form, not this term.
corrected: §5.6 and §29.1 price upkeep against a per-realm 'stability budget' that §5.5 never defines; capacity and strain are universe-wide. A realm's share must be defined. Candidates: its Anchor Stone's capacity, or the Spire for the Heart, with a rule for crown laws. The alternative is to price upkeep on the universe's strain.

title: The prototype gives the Heart the Spirit school, so Spirit laws get the realm-school discount there
evidence: screens_main.js:35: heart:{name:'The Heart',school:'Spirit',...}. Weaving applies ×0.8 when the law's school equals the realm's (screens_main.js:356). §5.2: 'Heart | Neutral | Circle | None'.
rec: Add to §23.5. The build follows §5.2: no realm-school discount at the Heart.
verdict_why: Confirmed. screens_main.js:35 has heart:{school:'Spirit'}, while §5.2 says 'Heart | Neutral | Circle | None'. wCostOf (:356) applies ×0.8 when the law's school matches the realm's, so Spirit laws show 20% cheaper at the Heart, and the school filter would read 'SPIRIT'. §23.5 does not list it. The document already wins, so the build follows §5.2.

title: Weaving's projection prices only the new law, without crown, resonance, chord or draw
evidence: screens_main.js:356 (wCostOf: tier, realm school, 0.85 per harmony, 1.25 per clash) and :361-362 (strain delta = new law ÷ a fixed capacity of 356). §5.5 line 845 has seven factors (crown ×2, resonance ×0.8, chord ×0.9 included), and strain adds every sounding chord's draw. §8.2 and §8.3 change both laws' cost.
rec: Note in §23.5 that the build prices weaving with one shared function (the client preview equals the server's charge) and never copies the prototype's arithmetic.
verdict_why: Confirmed. wCostOf (screens_main.js:356) uses tier, realm school, ×0.85 per harmony and ×1.25 per clash only. The strain change (:361-362) is the new law's cost over a fixed wCap of 356 (:357). It never re-prices the partner law (§8.2 says 'both laws'), and it leaves out resonance ×0.8, chord ×0.9 and chord draw (§5.5 line 845). §23.5's general rule (the document wins on rules) and its 'One data file' row (the prototype's module is not a source) already imply this, so the finding mainly warns against porting the prototype's arithmetic.

title: Hold to weave is fixed at one second, but §20.8 makes hold times adjustable
evidence: screens_main.js:424 (holdDown completes at p>=1 s) and a 110 px upward drag (:422). §20.8 (line 10300): 'nothing needs a fast tap, a double tap or a drag that can't also be done as two taps; ... hold times adjustable'. client/README.md: the client holds nothing, 'so there is no hold time to adjust'; Settings has no hold time.
rec: Add a hold-time setting before any hold ships and keep a two-tap path (select, then Weave). Add to §23.5.
verdict_why: Confirmed. Weaving's button binds only pointer-down and pointer-up (markup:621), and holdDown (screens_main.js:424) completes at a fixed 1 s. The alternative is a 110 px upward drag (dgUp). There is no tap path and no adjustable hold. §20.8 (line 10300) requires 'hold times adjustable' and that no drag be needed that cannot also be done as two taps. client/README.md:83 confirms the client has no holds today, so the build breaks nothing yet.

title: The Codex should count remaining resonances per school, and the document does not say how a two-school pair counts
evidence: §8.6 (line 4304): 'Once discovered; the Codex shows how many remain in each school'. The design shows one total, 2/12 (screens_meta.js:406). Most launch resonances join two schools: Mangrove banks is Time and Life, Night runners Time and Energy.
rec: State in §8.6 how a two-school resonance counts toward each school's remaining number, and list it in §23.5 as a design difference.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §8.6 (line 4304): 'the Codex shows how many remain in each school'. The design shows one total (ring 2/12, '1 hinted · 9 undiscovered', screens_meta.js:406). content/resonances.json shows most launch resonances join laws of two schools (Mangrove banks: Slow rivers Time + Bloom Life; Night runners: Haste Time + Glowing dark Energy), so a per-school count needs a rule.

title: What a crossing hint reveals is unstated
evidence: §8.4: 'hinted at after crossing them in someone else's universe'. §8.5: 'crossing one gives a hint'. No content is given. The design's hint names one law, the partner's school and where it was crossed ('You crossed this in Kofi's universe. Its partner is a Spirit law.', screens_meta.js:428). Its example also names a resonance that is not among the 12 launch ones.
rec: Write the hint's content in §8.6 (the design's form is a good default).
verdict_why: Confirmed. §8.4 and §8.6 say crossing gives a hint but never what it contains. The design's hint is 'You crossed this in Kofi's universe. Its partner is a Spirit law.' (screens_meta.js res list). For Stillness, its only Spirit-partner resonance is Frozen reflections (Mirror images), which is not a launch law, so the example points at a non-launch resonance. It implies it rather than names it.

title: Harmony view threads are not §21.7's pylon threads, jagged dissonance or turning chord triangle
evidence: §21.7 (line 10984): 'a thread in the note's colour links the two pylons; a dissonance is a jagged, flickering line; a chord forms a slowly turning triangle of light between three pylons.' The design draws beams between floating cards, a straight striped bar for a clash and a dashed triangle with marching dashes (screens_meta.js:1093-1100,1125).
rec: The build anchors threads to pylons and draws §21.7's shapes; add the row to §23.5.
verdict_why: Partly confirmed. §21.7 'Laws on screen' (line 10984) describes the in-world signature: a thread between the two pylons, a jagged flickering line for a dissonance, and a slowly turning triangle for a chord. It is not a spec for the Harmony view screen. The design draws harmonies only in the Harmony view, as beams between floating law cards. A clash there is a straight red-striped bar with a glow pulse, and a chord is a dashed triangle with marching dashes, not turning (screens_meta.js:1093-1100, triS). realm_diorama.js draws no harmony threads at all.
corrected: The designs draw no on-island harmony signature (§21.7: threads between pylons, a jagged flickering line for a dissonance, a slowly turning chord triangle). The Harmony view stands in with beams between cards, a straight striped bar for a clash and a marching-dash triangle. The build draws §21.7's in-world signatures, and the Harmony view may keep its own layout.

title: Codex notes (§15.3) appear in no screen design and are undefined
evidence: §15.3: 'Codex notes | What the player has seen each law do | Filled in automatically'. Neither the design's Codex (screens_meta.markup.html:167-180) nor its Law card has anything like it, and §23.2's Codex row does not list it.
rec: Define what is recorded (for example times crossed, what the law did to the crew, pylons broken) and add it to §23.2's Codex or Law card row.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §15.3 (line 8788) lists 'Codex notes | What the player has seen each law do | Filled in automatically', and no section defines them. The design's Codex (screens_meta.markup.html:167-180) and Law card back have nothing like it. §23.2's Codex row (line 11257) does not list them, so no must-show depends on them. This lowers the severity.

title: No rule chooses Weaving's two or three recommended laws or says what the comparison shows
evidence: §23.2 (line 11225) and §23.5 (line 11507) require 'Two or three recommended laws'; §19.6 (line 9468) adds 'with a comparison'. No section says how they are ranked (harmony and no clash, least strain, the realm's school, defence value). The design's deck sort (harmony first, clash last, then cheapest; screens_main.js:361) is one candidate.
rec: State the ranking and the comparison's fields in §5.6 or §23.2.
verdict_why: Confirmed. §23.2 (line 11225), §23.5 (line 11507) and §19.6 (line 9468, 'with a comparison') require two or three recommended laws, but no section says how they are chosen or what the comparison shows. §23.5's Weaving row records only that the design lacks them, not this gap in the document. title: Weaving edges left open: weaving into Breaking, re-weaving after a tier rise, one law in several realms
evidence: §5.5: 'Breaking ... No new weaving'. It does not say whether a weave may take strain from Cracking into Breaking; the design refuses it (screens_main.js:406). §7.6 prices tiers II and III but not what happens to a woven law when its tier rises. §5.1 forbids only 'both a crown law and a realm law'; the design lets Half gravity, woven in Skyfield, be woven at the Heart too.
rec: Add one line each to §5.5, §5.6 and §5.1.
verdict_why: Mostly confirmed. §5.5's Breaking band says 'No new weaving' but not whether a weave may push strain from Cracking into Breaking. The design blocks it ('Too much strain'). §7.6 prices tiers II and III, and §5.6 gives longer weave times, but nothing says whether a woven law upgrades in place or must be re-woven. The third edge is weaker. §5.1 forbids only crown-plus-realm, and by §23.5's adoption rule the design's choice to weave one law as a realm law in several realms is adopted where the document is silent and no rule breaks.
corrected: Two weaving edges are unstated: whether a weave may take strain into Breaking, and what happens to a woven law when its tier rises. The third, the same law woven in several realms, is not forbidden by §5.1 and falls under §23.5's adoption rule unless the owner wants it written down.
